files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Barks.BarkKind
files.Summary: What a soldier calls out. Every bark is triggered by a real decision or event, never by a timer, so listening to the squad tells the player what it's about to do.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Barks.BarkLog
files.Summary: The barks said during the current tick, like is for shots. It's cleared at the start of each AI update and read after the tick. The client shows barks as text until there's audio.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Barks.BarkRecord
files.Summary: One bark (a voice line a soldier called out).

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BehaviorAction
files.Summary: The actions a soldier can perform, each one a leaf of its behavior tree. The game decides how each is done (the soldier's movement, aim and tactics); the tree decides when.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BehaviorNode
files.Summary: One node of a compiled behavior tree.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BehaviorNodeKind
files.Summary: The type of a node in a soldier's behavior tree: how it decides whether it succeeds, and what it does.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BehaviorTree
files.Summary: A compiled soldier behavior tree. Holds the nodes reachable from the root, root first, with each node's children stored next to each other in .

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BodyAbilities
files.Summary: Data names for values, and which abilities each behavior tree action needs.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BodyAbility
files.Summary: Something a soldier's body has to be able to animate for its behavior to work. Behaviors never name animations, but a behavior that throws grenades needs a body that can visibly throw.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Behavior.SoldierBehavior
files.Summary: How a type of soldier behaves (content/defs/ai/<id>.json). Holds its behavior tree (what it does from moment to moment, from roaming to fighting) and the scoring the tree's "choose intent" action uses in a fight (hold, advance, push or fall back; ).

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Bots.MissionBot
files.Summary: A bot player that plays a mission on its own, for the Phase 3 gate (every seed has to be completable). It picks up the keycards in order (each one opens the gate to the next zone), walks to the terminal and holds Interact to start the hack, stays for it, then goes to extraction.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Choir.ChoirSpawner
files.Summary: Spawns the Choir's larger units along with their AI state ( drives them).

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Choir.ChoirSystem
files.Summary: The Choir's bigger bodies (): characters with a simple mind of their own, not a soldier's. Each goes for the nearest of anyone not of the Choir (players and soldiers alike), by the navigation grid or straight at them once in the open, and attacks after a wind-up that warns: Strippers close in and strike everyone and everything in front of them (cover and breakable walls included, going through what stands between them and their target); Spitters keep their distance and lob acid that leaves a burning pool (, ).

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Choir.ChoirTuning
files.Summary: Combat tuning for the Choir's larger units (). It's a record so tests and tools can make their own.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.ChoirBrain
files.Summary: The host-only AI state of a Choir unit ( is the part everyone sees). Holds its path to its target and what it last found between itself and the target.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.CoverRejects
files.Summary: Cover points (indices in the ) a soldier has ruled out for now: the way there passed too close to the enemy, or there was no way ().

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.DirectorPhase
files.Summary: The Director's current phase (design doc, "AI director"), modeled on Left 4 Dead's: build-up, peak, relax.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.DirectorState
files.Summary: The Director's state. It lives on a single entity, and each mission level has one.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.IntentReason
files.Summary: The consideration that weighed most in the chosen intent. This is the "why" the AI debugger shows.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.IntentScores
files.Summary: One utility score per .

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.PathPoints
files.Summary: A soldier's path, as its corner points in order.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.SoldierBrain
files.Summary: Everything a soldier's AI remembers between ticks. It's plain data so it can be inspected and checksummed.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.SoldierIntent
files.Summary: What a soldier fighting from cover plans to do next, picked by utility scoring (see ). The role is the soldier's job in the squad; the intent is how it's playing that job right now.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.SoldierState
files.Summary: What a soldier is doing.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.SoldierVariant
files.Summary: A soldier's enemy variant on the client side, as an index into . It's sent with each soldier so the client can draw the right model. On the host, soldiers keep this in their instead.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.SquadRole
files.Summary: A soldier's job in its squad, set by the squad coordinator.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.Stress
files.Summary: A player's stress level, read by the Director. It goes up when the player takes damage or gets downed, and fades when they're safe.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Components.TacticalInputs
files.Summary: The inputs a soldier used for its utility scores the last time it picked an intent. Kept for the debugger.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Director.AlertTuning
files.Summary: Tuning for the station's alert level (, 0 to 1): how it rises with time and noise, how little it drops, and how it affects the Director and the horde. This is a mission template's "alert" section.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Director.Difficulty
files.Summary: The run's difficulty. For now it only controls how early in a run the Choir's horde shows up and how fast it escalates.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Director.DirectorSystem
files.Summary: The Director (design doc, "AI director"). It reads how much pressure the squad is under and paces the fight around that, like Left 4 Dead's director.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Director.DirectorTuning
files.Summary: Director tuning values. Times are in seconds unless noted.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Director.RunPacing
files.Summary: Paces a mission based on how far into the run the squad is, counted as successful extractions in a row (a failed mission ends the run).

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Enemies.EnemyRoster
files.Summary: The enemy variants (content/defs/ai/enemies.json), and which one spawns where. A level's squads, the mission's reinforcements, the director's patrols and the Choir's squads each pick a variant using the weights the variants set for that source. The pick comes from the squad's seed, so it's the same on every machine.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Enemies.EnemySource
files.Summary: Where enemies come from. Each variant sets how often a squad from each source is made up of that variant.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Enemies.EnemyVariant
files.Summary: A type of enemy soldier (content/defs/ai/enemies.json): its body, guns, faction, the behavior it uses, and where it spawns. Every soldier in a squad is the same variant.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.CampaignTarget
files.Summary: Something the fleet can raid in a star system (content/defs/campaign.json): a station, or a ship of one of the plans.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.CampaignTuning
files.Summary: What the fleet finds to raid as it crosses the sectors (content/defs/campaign.json): stations, laid out by the station plans, and ships (frigates, carriers, strike carriers), each laid out by its plan, each turning up as often as its weight once the fleet has come far enough. Each system has a few of them (its points of interest), and a sector's first system and its gate always have a station first. A point raided is picked over: its cargo thinner, its guards heavier.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.FleetNeed
files.Summary: One line on the needs board: a supply, how many jumps the fleet's stock of it will last, and the text shown.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.FleetShip
files.Summary: One ship in the fleet: its kind, its name, how many people are aboard, and its condition (0 is lost, 100 is undamaged).

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.FleetSim
files.Summary: The fleet's simulation between missions (design doc, "The Fleet: home base" and "The Scourge at the strategic layer").

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.FleetState
files.Summary: The fleet's state between missions (design doc, "The Fleet: home base"): its ships and people, its stock of each supply, its morale, how many missions and jumps it has made, and how far behind the Scourge is.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.FleetVote
files.Summary: The squad's votes at the star map (design doc, "Co-op design": voting at the star map). Everyone picks a course, and the course is the one most of them picked. Everyone can vote to jump, and the fleet jumps once more than half the squad has. The host breaks ties: a course they picked wins a tie, and their vote to jump carries a split squad.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.Galaxy
files.Summary: The galaxy the fleet is running across (design doc, "Vast to look at, few choices to make"): a seeded spiral of stars, with every sector a region of it. The fleet starts near the core and runs outward along an arm, a sector at a time, so its trail leads back across everything it's crossed.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.GalaxyStar
files.Summary: One star of the galaxy behind the sectors, as the map draws it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.JumpTuning
files.Summary: How the fleet's jump plays out on the ship (campaign.json's jump): the countdown once the squad has voted, how far the lights go down while the drive spools up, and the flash and shake as it jumps.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.LockerItem
files.Summary: A weapon or a loose part in the armory's locker (design doc, "The armoury"). The locker is the fleet's, so it's everyone's: kept between missions, and anyone on the ship can take from it or put into it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.PointOfInterest
files.Summary: Somewhere in a star system the squad can drop to (design doc, "Jumping and points of interest"): a station, or a ship of one of the plans. Holds its seed and the settings it's generated with: how heavily it's guarded and what its cargo is mostly made of.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.ShipKind
files.Summary: A fleet ship's role (design doc, "Ships and modules").

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.StarMap
files.Summary: Builds and queries the sector the fleet is crossing (design doc, "Map structure"). A sector has ten to fourteen systems from its entry (on the left) to its gate (on the right). Each is linked to its nearest neighbors so there are alternate routes, and each has a few points of interest to drop to, stations and ships.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.StarSystem
files.Summary: A star system in the sector the fleet is crossing (design doc, "Star map"). Holds its map position, its lanes, and its points of interest: the stations and ships there the squad can drop to.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Fleet.SystemKnowledge
files.Summary: What the fleet knows of a star system (design doc, "Knowledge states"). The map shows each differently: what can't be seen is the point.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Horde.HordeField
files.Summary: One flow field for the whole horde (design doc, "Horde simulation"). Instead of a path per swarmling, every spot in the level knows which direction leads to the nearest player.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Horde.HordeSystem
files.Summary: The horde (design doc, "Horde simulation"): the Choir's swarmlings, hundreds at once. Not characters: no controller, no physics body, no brain. Each runs over the navigation grid down one shared towards the nearest player, straight at them once close and in the open, keeps apart from the others by a spatial hash, and lunges: a short wind-up (the telegraph) and a bite. Shots and grenades kill them (the shot and grenade systems test bodies) and knock them back; the dead lie a moment and are gone.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Horde.HordeTuning
files.Summary: How the horde moves, attacks and spawns (design doc, "Horde simulation"). Times are in seconds, lengths in meters.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.BattleStations
files.Summary: A boarded warship's crew at battle stations (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"; boarding.crew in campaign.json): the ship knows it's been boarded the moment the pod clamps on, so it never drops below high alert, every soldier is on the move between rooms rather than standing at a post, hunters are sent sooner and given no breathers, and they push the squad harder once they find it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.BoardingPlan
files.Summary: A boarding action's warship (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): where its gun batteries, its reactor and its fire suppression controls are, how the fight outside goes (how often the fleet's guns hit it, what a hit does, how fires spread and are put out, how hard its batteries hit the fleet), and how its crew fights.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.BreachPlan
files.Summary: A hull breach (HullBreaches): the plate that covers it, the plate's bounds, and which direction points into the room.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.BreachTuning
files.Summary: How windows onto space break and what a breach does (content/defs/breaches.json, docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10), the same for every mission: how much a window takes before it's blown out and when its cracks show, how hard and how far the air rushing out pulls, what it does to anyone beside it and what it drags out, and how long the compartment's doors take to seal, the shutter to close and the compartment to repressurize; and how it looks (the shutter's drop, the mist streaming out, the lamps over sealed doors). Whether a breach is for good is the mission recipe's (its breaches block).

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.BulkheadPlan
files.Summary: A door through a bulkhead that seals (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 8): the level part that fills its doorway, its bounds, and the compartments either side of it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.CargoPodSystem
files.Summary: Runs cargo pod defenses (). Once the drone is called, it takes longer to arrive the deeper into the station the squad is (), and the station comes for the pod.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.ClosetPlan
files.Summary: A spawn closet: its door part and bounds, the spots where soldiers spawn inside, and the closet's interior bounds.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.EscapePodPlan
files.Summary: An escape pod: the level part (surface) of its hatch and the hatch's bounds, the middle of the pod inside, and how many it seats.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.FirePanel
files.Summary: A boarded warship's fire suppression panel (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): holding Interact at it floods its room while it burns, putting the fire out.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.MissionKeyPlan
files.Summary: A keycard placed in the level. It opens the lock with the same id.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.MissionLockPlan
files.Summary: A locked door: the level part (surface) that fills its doorway, plus its bounds.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.MissionPlan
files.Summary: A level's mission layout: keycards and locks, the terminal, the extraction point, spawn closets, fallback points where reinforcements can enter when no closet works, hull breaches the horde can come through, and fuel and water tanks to pump into the docked dropship.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.MissionSystem
files.Summary: A boarding action (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): the warship the squad is on is in a fight with the fleet. The fleet's guns hit it on a cadence (each hit counted in , so everyone aboard feels it); a hit hurts those near it, and sometimes starts a fire or blows a window. Fires spread room to room and burn out, unless the ship's fire suppression is running: its sprinklers put them out, until a hit knocks it out (repaired at its controls in damage control) or its power goes (cutting the reactor kills it). While its batteries fire, the fleet takes damage. The squad silences the batteries and cuts the reactor by holding Interact at each, then takes the bridge; a battery or the reactor lost with its room to a breach is out for good.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.MissionTuning
files.Summary: Mission tuning values. Distances are in meters, times in seconds.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.MissionWalk
files.Summary: Whether the mission can still be finished with some compartments, or rooms, lost (docs/plans/structure-first.md, decision 8): from the insertion, through doorways whose rooms are both kept, each gate passable once its keycard's room has been reached and the way out once the objective has, can the objective and then an extraction be reached? A breach seals its compartment for good only when this holds without it and every compartment already lost, so two losses can never together lock the squad out, and keycards stay reachable whatever is sealed.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.ObjectivePlan
files.Summary: What a mission's squad comes for and how long it takes (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "Objective kinds"): the hack, a download whose drive is carried out, or a self-destruct counted down while the squad gets off.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.PatrolRoomPlan
files.Summary: A room the Director's patrols can come out of when no spawn closet will do (a security office, crew quarters): only while nobody is in it, near its spots or can see one, its zone open and its compartment unsealed.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.ReinforcementPoint
files.Summary: A spawn point for reinforcements, with a yaw that faces into the level.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.RoomDoorPlan
files.Summary: A room's own door in a plan's level, as the mission runs it (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10): its part, the rooms either side, and whether it's opened by hand or slides open for whoever comes near.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.RoomDoorTuning
files.Summary: How rooms' own doors behave (content/defs/doors.json, docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10), the same for every mission: how near someone comes for a sliding door to open and how long it waits to shut behind them; how near a player reaches a door opened by hand, and how long a soldier takes to open one on his way; and how much battering a door opened by hand takes from the swarm before it's broken open for good.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.SuppressionControls
files.Summary: A boarded warship's fire suppression controls (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"), in its damage control: while the system runs, the ship's sprinklers put its fires out; a hit can knock it out, and holding Interact here repairs it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.TankPlan
files.Summary: A fuel or water tank in the mission (), with its starting state.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.TankPumpSystem
files.Summary: Pumps supply tanks () into the docked dropship. Whatever gets pumped belongs to the fleet immediately (), even if the mission fails afterward.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.ThreatPlan
files.Summary: How hard a level's places are defended (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "Threat drives the fight"), and the patrols that sets. While the squad is in a room, its threat sets how often the Director sends a patrol and how big, the station's alert speeding both on top.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Missions.WindowPlan
files.Summary: A window onto space, as the mission's breaches need it (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10): its parts by surface, where its pane is, the compartment it lets space into, and whether that may ever be lost.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Navigation.NavClusters
files.Summary: A coarse map over a for long paths. Each 4 m square of each floor is split into clusters of walkable cells that connect inside the square, and clusters are linked wherever a link or a drop crosses from one to the next.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Navigation.NavGrid
files.Summary: A layered navigation grid over a level. Each column of the grid holds every floor in it, from the ground up to mezzanines, catwalks and stair landings, so floors stacked over each other are all navigable.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Navigation.NavGridSettings
files.Summary: How a is sampled from the level.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Navigation.NavTopology
files.Summary: The parts of a 's navigation that never change once it's built: each cell's column coordinates and the cluster map (). There's one per grid (), shared by every on it, which each keep only their own search memory.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Navigation.PathSearchStats
files.Summary: Counts of path searches, summed over some period (one tick, a run): how many, how many found no way, how many fell back to the whole grid, how many cells they expanded and how long they took. For the developer overlay and the headless benchmark; the simulation never reads it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Navigation.Pathfinder
files.Summary: A* over a . Eight-connected with no corner cutting, goes between floors via stairs and ramps and down ledges via drop links, then smooths the result into straight segments. All working memory is allocated up front, so finding a path doesn't allocate.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Navigation.ShutDoors
files.Summary: Keeps a out of doorways that are still shut. The nav grid is built with every door open, so this blocks the mission's locked doors (except the ones the pathing agent can open), the spawn closet doors, and the doors through bulkheads shut for a seal (), which nobody opens. It only rebuilds when a door opens or shuts.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.AiSection
files.Summary: A part of 's tick, timed separately (). Together they are the whole tick.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.CoverWork
files.Summary: What choosing cover cost in a tick (): how many choices, the cover points they looked at, the claim checks against other soldiers' cover, and the ray tests. For the developer overlay and the headless benchmark; the simulation never reads it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.PathPurpose
files.Summary: What a soldier's path search was for, to count the searches by ().

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.SightWork
files.Summary: What looking for enemies cost in a tick (): how many soldiers looked, the characters they looked over, how many enemies were in view and range, and the sight lines cast to them. For the developer overlay and the headless benchmark; the simulation never reads it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.SoldierAiSystem
files.Summary: Barks, and picking an intent through utility scoring.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.SoldierArms
files.Summary: Picks the guns soldiers carry. Each soldier's gun is derived from its seed, so the host and every client agree.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.SoldierSpawner
files.Summary: Spawns soldiers with their AI. Each one is an enemy variant (), which sets its body, guns, faction and the behavior it uses.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.SoldierTuning
files.Summary: How tough soldiers are to fight. Difficulty comes from reactions, aim and coordination, never from health (see the Difficulty table in the design doc).

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.SoldierTunings
files.Summary: Soldier tuning per faction: the values every faction shares (), plus separate values for any faction that differs ().

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.TuningField
files.Summary: One soldier tuning value (): its key in tuning.json, how it's shown and edited, and how it's read from and written to a tuning. The developer overlay, LastFleet Studio and the file all go through , so they always agree on which fields exist.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.TuningFields
files.Summary: Every soldier tuning value (), grouped the way they're edited. This is the list of what tuning.json can hold and what the developer overlay and LastFleet Studio show, with slider ranges and a description of each.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.TuningKind
files.Summary: The type of value a holds, which decides how it's saved and edited.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Tactics.CoverMap.Nearby
files.Summary: Enumerates the points in the squares around a spot, square by square. See .

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Tactics.CoverMap
files.Summary: Cover points found in the level once, at load time: walkable spots next to walls and obstacles, tested with horizontal rays at crouching and standing height.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Tactics.CoverPoint
files.Summary: A place to take cover: a walkable spot with something solid on one side.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Tactics.LightMap
files.Summary: Tracks where the station is dark, so soldiers know when to turn on their flashlights. Holds each room's lights, minus the ones that are dead or shot out. A point counts as dark when its room's working lights barely reach it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Tactics.RoomCells
files.Summary: A room's cells on the layout grid: the corner and size of its bounding box, its lowest story and how many stories it spans. For a room that doesn't fill its box (an L or U shape), it also lists the cells it does fill.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Tactics.RoomDoor
files.Summary: A doorway between two rooms. Holds the doorway's center at floor level and the horizontal direction from room A into room B.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Tactics.RoomLight
files.Summary: A working light in a room, for .

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Tactics.RoomMap
files.Summary: A generated level's rooms and the doorways between them, so soldiers can fight indoors. Answers which room a point is in, which doorways lead out of a room, and the route from room to room.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Tactics.TacticalUtility
files.Summary: Utility scoring for what a soldier in a fight does next: hold its cover, advance, push the enemy, or fall back. Uses the shipped data (, content/defs/ai/soldier.json) with the first personality, a steady squad.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Utility.IntentRule
files.Summary: How one intent gets scored ().

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Utility.Personality
files.Summary: A squad's personality: a scale on each intent's score (a bold squad pushes more, a cautious one falls back sooner), plus how often squads get it.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Utility.UtilityCompare
files.Summary: How a condition compares its input with its value.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Utility.UtilityCondition
files.Summary: A test on one input, for example "range < 22" or "role != retreat".

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Utility.UtilityCurve
files.Summary: Maps an input to a value, in one of two ways.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Utility.UtilityFactor
files.Summary: A multiplier applied to an intent's score after its terms are added up. The value comes from its curve and/or its value for the soldier's role (1 for a role that isn't listed). It only applies when its conditions hold.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Utility.UtilityInput
files.Summary: The inputs a soldier's curves and conditions can read when it scores its intents.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Utility.UtilityModel
files.Summary: How soldiers decide what to do in a fight (a behavior's scoring, content/defs/ai/soldier.json): utility scoring of hold, advance, push and fall back. Each intent's score is its base plus its terms, times its factors (), times the squad personality's scale for it. The highest score wins, with the current intent getting added on top.

files.Title: LastFleet.AI.Utility.UtilityTerm
files.Summary: A value added to an intent's score: times its curve (1 if there's no curve) times its weight for the soldier's role (1 if there are no role weights, 0 for a role that isn't listed). It only applies when its conditions hold.

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.AudioEngine
files.Summary: Plays sounds through OpenAL Soft.

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.ISoundOutput
files.Summary: Where the game sends the sounds it wants played. That's , or a recorder in tests.

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.PlaceholderSounds
files.Summary: Stand-in sounds generated in code for everything the game plays, until a recording replaces them (a .wav in content/sounds, see docs/sound.md).

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.RoomAcoustics
files.Summary: The kind of space the listener is in, for the reverb.

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.SoundCategory
files.Summary: Which volume setting controls a sound.

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.SoundClip
files.Summary: One recording (or placeholder) of a cue, as mono samples from -1 to 1.

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.SoundCue
files.Summary: How a sound plays, as defined in content/defs/sounds.json: how loud it is, how far it carries, whether it's placed in the world, and how many copies can play at once.

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.SoundLibrary
files.Summary: Every sound the game can play. Holds the cues (content/defs/sounds.json) and each cue's clips. The clips are the recordings in content/sounds (name.wav, name_2.wav, ...), or the cue's placeholder () until recordings exist. Each play picks one of the cue's clips at random.

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.VoicePool
files.Summary: Picks which of a fixed set of voices plays each new sound. Doesn't allocate.

files.Title: LastFleet.Audio.WavFile
files.Summary: Reads and writes .wav files. Reads PCM 8, 16, 24 or 32-bit, or 32-bit float, mixed down to one channel.

files.Title: LastFleet.Client.Fleet.Armory
files.Summary: The armory's workbench and locker (design doc, "The armoury"): the rules for what the squad does with the fleet's weapons and parts between missions. Store and take, fit and remove parts at once, dismantle into raw material for the refinery, rework with refined material, and fabricate into the locker.

files.Title: LastFleet.Client.Fleet.LockerHands
files.Summary: Between the armory's locker and what a player carries (design doc, "The armoury"): the weapon in their hands or a part from their pack into the locker, or something from the locker into their hands or pack. The host does it on its world, so everyone sees it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Client.Fleet.Refinery
files.Summary: The fleet's refinery and the armory's fabricator, driven by the loot data (grades, refinery tiers, recipes, fabrication). Raw materials brought back go into the fleet's stores (). Each jump the refinery turns them into graded material, as many batches as its tier allows, in the grades it can make. Upgrading the refinery costs fleet supplies. The fabricator spends graded material on a weapon or a part at the grade's item level.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.ContentFingerprint
files.Summary: A stable hash of the content the game generates and plays missions from. Co-op peers use it to check they have the same data before playing. A level is sent as just its seed, so two peers with different data would build different levels from it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Creatures.AnimatedMesh
files.Summary: One level of detail of an : flat-shaded triangles (three vertices each, none shared), with every vertex's position and face normal on every frame of every animation.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Creatures.AnimatedModel
files.Summary: A creature made and animated in Blender (content/models, docs/blender/creatures.md): its meshes skinned to an armature and its actions, baked when loaded into where every vertex is on every frame, so the GPU can draw hundreds of them at once, each on its own frame, with no skinning of its own.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Creatures.AnimationClip
files.Summary: One animation of an (a Blender action), baked to frames.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Encounters.BreakableLayout
files.Summary: Finds breakable props in a level by part name: every part named Break_*.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Encounters.BreakablePart
files.Summary: A breakable prop found in a level mesh.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Encounters.EncounterLayout
files.Summary: A level's encounter, read from the .encounter.json file next to its module: where the player spawns, the soldier squads, and the ammo crates.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Encounters.SpawnLayout
files.Summary: Where a character spawns: the position of its feet and its facing. A yaw of 0 faces down -Z.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Encounters.SquadLayout
files.Summary: A squad of soldiers that fight together.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Encounters.TargetLayout
files.Summary: Finds practice targets in a level by part name. Target_ is a body, and Target__Head is its head.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Encounters.TargetParts
files.Summary: A practice target found in a level mesh: its body part, plus its head part if it has one.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Forge.ForgeFile
files.Summary: Writes forged parts () out as a weapon part file (content/weapons/*.gltf, see docs/blender/weapons.md), in the same layout the Blender add-on and the greybox kit used.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Forge.ForgeMarker
files.Summary: A named empty on a forged part (), for example a socket, a hand position, a muzzle or a sight.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Forge.ForgeMaterial
files.Summary: A material used by a forged part (). It has a preview color and a surface material from the library (content/defs/materials.json).

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Forge.ForgePart
files.Summary: A weapon part as the forge builds it (docs/plans/weapons.md phase 5). It has the name the game looks for (Receiver, Barrel_0_Plain), its triangles in its own space (with the origin at the attach point), and its markers. adds shapes to it, and writes parts out as glTF.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Forge.ForgeRecipes
files.Summary:
The weapon parts' recipes (content/weapons/forge.json; docs/plans/weapons.md phase 5): for each part file (a frame's, and shared), each part's shapes and markers, which the forge builds into the part files the game reads (). A recipe's shapes, each one object naming its kind by its first key:

  • box: its center; size (whole, not half); bevel its edges' cut; turn degrees about x, y, z.
  • prism: one end, to the other; r its radius; sides (8); bevel.
  • tube: one end, to the other; r outside, inner inside; sides (12).
  • rail: one end, to the other; width; up its top's way ([0, 1, 0]); pitch its ridges'.
  • vents: the first's center; along the row's way; facing the face's; count; step; size each (along, deep, across).
  • bolt: its head's center; facing; r.
  • block: its eight corners, as a box's (x fastest, then y, then z).

Each takes m, its material (; Body by default), and detail (true for the small things only your own gun shows: ). A part's markers name points: its sockets, hands' places, muzzle, sight.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Forge.ForgeShapes
files.Summary: The shapes forged parts are built from (docs/plans/weapons.md phase 5). These are what make low-poly parts look manufactured instead of just boxy.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Forge.ForgeTriangle
files.Summary: One triangle of a forged part (), wound counter-clockwise when seen from outside.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Images.ImageRgba
files.Summary: An image stored as 8-bit RGBA pixels, with rows ordered top to bottom.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Images.PngReader
files.Summary: Decodes the PNG files the game ships, such as logos and UI art: 8 bits per channel, greyscale or color, with or without alpha, not interlaced. Anything else is rejected with a clear message rather than decoded wrongly.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Loading.GltfJson
files.Summary: Reads the raw JSON of a .gltf or .glb file, for data BRUTAL's glTF API doesn't keep: extras (Blender's custom properties) on nodes and materials.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Loading.GltfMeshLoader
files.Summary: Loads a glTF level module into one flat-shaded, world-space , ready to draw and to build collision from.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Materials.FixtureGlow
files.Summary: Works out how bright a light fixture's glass glows. A light and the glass it shines from are treated as one thing, so the glass takes the light's color, and its brightness is the light's strength spread over the glass area (a small lens on the same light glows brighter than a long panel).

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Materials.MaterialLibrary
files.Summary: The surface materials every model is drawn with (content/defs/materials.json). It's a fixed library, tuned in Studio and picked in Blender, so paint looks like paint on every gun, prop and wall. Each vertex stores its material's index into this library (), and the renderer reads the library as a table.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Materials.SightWindow
files.Summary: What a sight's glass shows (): the reticle of a red dot or holographic sight. It's drawn only where the eye looks along the aim (as if projected at infinity). The rest of the glass is clear.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Materials.SurfaceMaterial
files.Summary: A material in the library (content/defs/materials.json, see ). It describes how a surface reacts to light. The color comes from the model; the material says whether it's paint or bare metal, rough or polished.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Meshes.BoxFit
files.Summary: Detects whether a mesh part is a box, possibly rotated. That's the only shape level collision supports.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Meshes.MaterialColors
files.Summary: Works out the color a glTF material is drawn in: its base color plus its emission times the emission strength (KHR_materials_emissive_strength, which Blender exports when Emission is stronger than 1). This lets a lamp, a screen or an engine glow be brighter than white, which the renderer shows as glowing.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Meshes.MeshData
files.Summary: A static, world-space triangle mesh, stored as an indexed triangle list with counter-clockwise front faces.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Meshes.MeshPart
files.Summary: A named range of triangles inside a . It's one glTF node, such as one wall or one crate.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Meshes.MeshVertex
files.Summary: One vertex of a static world mesh, laid out exactly as the GPU reads it (40 bytes).

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Meshes.SmoothNormals
files.Summary: Computes smoothed normals for the corners of flat triangles, used for smooth materials' highlights ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Meshes.VertexSurface
files.Summary: Packs a vertex's surface data into 32 bits, the way the shaders read it. The lowest byte is the library material (). For a smooth material, the next three bytes hold the smoothed normal as a signed byte each for x, y and z. A zero normal means there isn't one, and highlights follow the face like everything else.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ColliderKind
files.Summary: What a model is collided with wherever it's placed (content/props/colliders.json, ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.LibraryModel
files.Summary: One model in the : a top-level object from a file in content/props or content/weapons.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelColliders
files.Summary: What each model is collided with (), read from colliders.json next to the models (content/props). Kept apart from the models themselves and from the rules that place them, since the same model is placed by many rules.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelFile
files.Summary: One .gltf file in the , and the models in it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelId
files.Summary: The id data uses to refer to a model: its file in content/props or content/weapons (without .gltf) and the top-level object in it, written as "file/Object" (items/Medkit, auto_rifle/Receiver).

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelKind
files.Summary: Which folder a model in the comes from. This decides which game colors it can use.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelLibrary
files.Summary: Every model made in Blender for the game: each top-level object of each .gltf in content/props and content/weapons, named "file/Object" (), with its paint slots.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelMarker
files.Summary: An empty inside a , for example a socket, a muzzle or an aim point.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelMaterial
files.Summary: A material on a model: its name, base color and which library material it maps to.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelPart
files.Summary: One top-level object in a parts file (): its triangles and empties, in its own space. The origin of that space is the attach point.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelParts
files.Summary: Loads a glTF file of parts (weapon parts made in Blender). Each top-level object is a part, with its meshes and empties in its own space.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.ModelTriangle
files.Summary: A triangle of a , in the part's own space, with the material it uses.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.PaintSlot
files.Summary: A part of a model whose color is set by the data. In Blender it's a material named Paint_<Name> (see ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.PaintSlots
files.Summary: The naming rules for model materials and color (see docs/blender/props.md and docs/blender/weapons.md). A material named Paint_<Name> is a whose color is set by the data, defaulting to the material's own color. A few names are colored by the game (a prop's Glint, a gun's Body). Any other material keeps its own color.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.PartShape
files.Summary: The body a level part with one () is collided with, from its triangles. Rays always hit the triangles themselves.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Models.PartUsage
files.Summary: Whether a part is drawn, collided with, or both.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Reloads.MagazinePlace
files.Summary: Where the magazine is during a reload step ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Reloads.ReloadLibrary
files.Summary: The reload definitions (content/defs/reloads.json; see docs/plans/weapons.md phase 4). For each frame model, it holds the steps its guns' reloads go through, if any. A frame without one keeps the body's own reload clip, with the hand off the gun.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Reloads.ReloadPoint
files.Summary: Where a reload step moves the left hand to ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Reloads.ReloadPose
files.Summary: The state of a reload at one point in time, as returned by . It holds the two points the hand is moving between, how far along it is (eased, 0 to 1), and where the magazine is.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Reloads.ReloadScript
files.Summary: How guns of certain frames reload (content/defs/reloads.json, ): the left hand's steps over the course of the reload, and where the magazine is during each one.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Reloads.ReloadStep
files.Summary: One step of a reload (): the hand moves to a point and gets there by a given fraction of the reload.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.Rig
files.Summary: A rig: the skeleton bodies of one kind are modeled and animated on (content/rigs/<id>.json; the humanoid first): its bones in their rest pose, the sockets the game uses, the chains IK solves, the masks layers of animation cover, the simulation's numbers the body is fitted to, and the clips made for it. A rig is data, so a four- or eight-legged body is a file, not code. The Blender add-on (tools/blender/lastfleet_rigs.py) builds the rig from the same file and checks models and their animations against it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigBody
files.Summary: The simulation's body measurements that a rig's body is fitted to.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigBone
files.Summary: A bone of a , in its rest pose.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigChain
files.Summary: A chain of bones that IK solves from root to tip, for example an arm, a leg, or the spine and head.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigChainTarget
files.Summary: What an IK chain reaches for.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigClip
files.Summary: An animation made for a rig, identified by name.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigEye
files.Summary: Where a clip keeps the body's eye. It's either pinned to where the simulation puts it for standing or crouched (so the head is where shots hit and the first-person camera lines up), or free (falling dead, downed, leaning out).

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigMask
files.Summary: The set of bones an animation layer affects, for example the upper body or the arms. Bones are indices in .

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigSocket
files.Summary: A named point on a bone that the game uses, for example where the first-person camera sits or where a hand holds the gun.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigTranslation
files.Summary: Where a bone's offset from its parent comes from when a clip plays on a model of the rig (like Unreal's bone translation retargeting). This lets models on the same rig have different builds, such as longer arms or a shorter body, and still share its clips.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.ClipSet
files.Summary: A rig's clips (content/anim/<rig>.gltf: the armature and its actions, made in Blender), bound to a skeleton by joint name so every model of the rig can play them. Channels for joints the skeleton doesn't have are dropped.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph.AnimAction
files.Summary: A one-shot animation a body plays on top of whatever else it's doing (like Unreal's montage played into a slot), for example a reload, a throw or a shot's kick.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph.AnimEvent
files.Summary: A named moment in a clip (a footstep, the magazine coming out) that an passed during a frame.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph.AnimGraph
files.Summary: A body type's animation graph, read from content/anim/<id>.json. It has the parameters it reads, and a tree of nodes (clips, blend spaces, selects, masked layers, additives, and IK for reaching, looking and foot placement) that turns those parameters into a pose. It's shared by every model of its rig.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph.AnimInstance
files.Summary: One body playing an . It holds the body's parameters, which get set every frame before evaluation, and the per-body state the graph keeps between frames (each clip's clock, each synced blend's phase, which state each select node picked and how far it has faded to it). Create one per body; evaluating it doesn't allocate.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph.AnimParameter
files.Summary: A number an reads. The code that knows the body's state (the client's bridge from the simulation) sets it for each body every frame. Flags are numbers too: 1 for on, 0 for off.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph.AnimPlayer
files.Summary: An bound to a model's skeleton and the rig's clips. It poses any number of bodies (each an ), one at a time, without allocating. Not thread-safe.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph.ClipChoice
files.Summary: Decides which actual clip plays for each clip a graph names, for one grip style and one enemy variant (like Unreal's per-item animation layers, the way Lyra gives each weapon its own). The graph stays a single template for every body of its type, and whoever plays it swaps in their own clips. Created by and assigned to a body's .

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph.ClipEvent
files.Summary: An event defined in a graph (like Unreal's notify). It marks a moment on a clip node (in seconds into the clip) or in an action (as a fraction, 0 to 1), and says what happens when a body passes it: a sound to play, an effect to show, and where on the body.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph.IAnimWorld
files.Summary: What a body's IK nodes query from the world while its graph plays: where its targets are (the grips of the gun it holds) and where the ground is under its feet. Everything is in the body's model space: feet at the origin, +Y up, facing -Z. The game passes this to . Without one, IK nodes do nothing.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.JointPoint
files.Summary: A point attached to a joint and bound to a skeleton, such as a rig socket (where a hand holds the gun, where the eye is). It stores the joint and the point in the joint's own space.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.JointTransform
files.Summary: A joint's transform relative to its parent: translation, rotation and scale.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Pose
files.Summary: The transform of every joint of a relative to its parent, from one sampled clip or several blended together. Create it once and reuse it every frame; nothing here allocates.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.PoseIk
files.Summary: Inverse kinematics on a : a two-bone chain (an arm, a leg) reaching for a point, rotating a chain (the spine and head looking up), and moving a joint (dropping the hips).

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.RigFit
files.Summary: Checks whether a model fits its rig: it must have the rig's bones under the same parents, and its eye must be where the simulation expects it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.SkeletalClip
files.Summary: One of a rig's clips (an action made in Blender), bound to a . It holds the keys for each joint it moves. It can be sampled into a at any time, interpolating between keys, so it plays at any rate.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Skeleton
files.Summary: The joints that drive a skinned model (a glTF skin: the armature made in Blender on a rig), ordered so each comes after its parent. It holds their names, their rest pose relative to their parents, and the inverse bind matrices that take a vertex from model space to each joint.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.SkinnedModel
files.Summary: A character made in Blender on a rig (content/characters, see docs/blender/rigs.md). Its meshes are skinned to the rig's skeleton and stored as flat triangles in the bind pose, each vertex with its four joints and weights, so the GPU can skin it every frame using the pose the game provides.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.SkinnedVertex
files.Summary: A vertex of a skinned model in its rest (bind) pose, laid out the way the GPU reads it. It holds the position, the face normal (faces are flat), the color, the four joints that move it with their weights, and its surface data.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skies.SkyBand
files.Summary: A sky's dust band: the galaxy's disc seen edge on, a glowing band of stars and dust round the sky ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skies.SkyLibrary
files.Summary: The skies windows show (content/defs/skies.json): each a , and the order the fleet meets them in, one a sector (), going round again past the last. Tuned in Studio's Look mode.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skies.SkyLook
files.Summary: A sky as the renderer draws it, for one place: a turned for where in the sector the fleet is (). Colors are linear and scaled by their strengths; directions are unit vectors in world space.

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skies.SkyNebula
files.Summary: A sky's nebula: clouds of glowing gas, shading from in their thick parts to at their edges ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skies.SkyStars
files.Summary: A sky's stars: how many, how bright, and their tint ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skies.SkySun
files.Summary: A sky's star: the sector's sun, a bright disc with a glow round it ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Content.Skies.SpaceSky
files.Summary: A sector's sky (content/defs/skies.json, ): the dark of space, its stars, a nebula, the galaxy's dust band and the sector's sun. Windows show it (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 9). Where in the sector the fleet is turns it (), so the sun stands elsewhere at each system.

files.Title: LastFleet.Core.Determinism.DeterministicRandom
files.Summary: A seeded pseudo-random generator (xoshiro256**) that produces the same sequence on every machine.

files.Title: LastFleet.Core.Determinism.RandomState
files.Summary: A snapshot of a 's 256-bit state.

files.Title: LastFleet.Core.Determinism.StableHash
files.Summary: Hash functions whose results never change between runs, machines, operating systems or .NET versions.

files.Title: LastFleet.Core.Timing.FixedTimestep
files.Summary: Converts variable-length render frames into a whole number of fixed simulation ticks ("fix your timestep").

files.Title: LastFleet.Core.Timing.FrameLimiter
files.Summary: Caps the frame rate at a maximum FPS so the GPU doesn't do needless work or cause coil whine.

files.Title: LastFleet.Ecs.GameWorld
files.Summary: One simulation world: an entity store plus systems that run in a fixed order every tick.

files.Title: LastFleet.Ecs.ISimulationSystem
files.Summary: A unit of simulation logic that runs once per fixed tick.

files.Title: LastFleet.Ecs.TickContext
files.Summary: Everything a system needs to know about the tick it is running.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.Affix
files.Summary: A prefix ("Overclocked") or suffix ("of the Vigil") that can roll onto weapons of high enough rarity.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.Fabrication
files.Summary: Something the armory can fabricate from graded material (the "fabrication" data). It's either a weapon rolled from a loot table or a weapon part (for one slot or any slot). The item level comes from the grade it costs.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.FabricationKind
files.Summary: What a makes.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.ItemTable
files.Summary: What a pile, container or cargo crate holds (content/defs/loot/items.json, "itemTables"). A roll picks one entry by weight, plus a count.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.ItemTableEntry
files.Summary: One entry in an : an item, how likely it is to be picked, and how many drop.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.LootArchetype
files.Summary: A weapon frame for loot rolls: the simulation's , the 0–100 stats a roll starts from, and the bounds every stat gets clamped to at the end.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.LootColor
files.Summary: A HUD color, parsed from a #rrggbb value in the data.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.LootEntry
files.Summary: One weighted entry in a loot table. It can only drop between its min and max item levels.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.LootEntryKind
files.Summary: What a loot table entry drops.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.LootStat
files.Summary: A stat that a weapon part, manufacturer or affix can change. The first five are 0–100 stats. The rest are scales on the frame's damage, magazine or zoom (see ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.LootTable
files.Summary: A loot table: weighted entries (archetypes, nested tables, relics), plus biases on the rarity and manufacturer odds. The biases multiply down through nested tables.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.Manufacturer
files.Summary: A weapon manufacturer: its stat bias, which applies to every gun it makes, and its model names per archetype. A manufacturer with no model for an archetype doesn't make that archetype.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.MaterialGrade
files.Summary: A grade of refined material (the "grades" data: Mk I, Mk II, ...). The fleet's refinery makes it from raw materials, and the armory uses it to fabricate items. A higher grade gives a higher item level.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.Rarity
files.Summary: A rarity tier. Its chance is × (1 + × (item level − 1)), times the loot table's bias. So higher item levels shift the odds toward rarer tiers.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.RefineryRecipe
files.Summary: A refinery recipe for turning raw materials into a material grade (the "recipes" data). One batch uses Inputs and produces Count of Grade.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.RefineryTier
files.Summary: One upgrade level of the fleet's refinery (the "refineryTiers" data, lowest first). A fleet starts at the first tier. Each tier has an upgrade cost paid from the fleet's stores, the grades it can make, and how many batches it refines per jump.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.Relic
files.Summary: A hand-authored unique weapon with a fixed archetype, manufacturer, parts and affixes. Every range rolls at its best value.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.ReworkRules
files.Summary: How the armory's workbench reworks what's in the locker (crafting.json's "rework"), paid in refined material. A weapon is reworked to a higher item level: the same roll, its stats at the new level, paid in the grade that makes things of that level. A part is tuned: its ranges roll better, paid in the grade of its rarity.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.SalvageYield
files.Summary: What the armory's workbench gets from dismantling a weapon or a part of one rarity (crafting.json's "salvage"): raw materials, by item id, which go to the fleet's stores for the refinery.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.StatRange
files.Summary: One stat change and the range it rolls in. If is false, it adds whole points to a 0–100 stat. If it's true, it multiplies the stat or scale. Additions are applied before multiplications.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.WeaponPart
files.Summary: A weapon part in a slot's pool.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.WeaponPartSlot
files.Summary: The part slots on a weapon (see the design doc, "Weapon anatomy"). The first five are the original slots. Muzzle, grip and trigger were added later. They roll after everything else, each from its own random stream, so adding them didn't change any weapon rolled before (see ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Drops.LootSystem
files.Summary: Handles soldier weapon and kit drops. When a soldier (anything with a ) dies, it can drop a weapon where it fell, and next to it a medkit or ammo pack, or a weapon part (each with its own separate roll).

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Drops.SoldierLoot
files.Summary: What soldiers drop. Each soldier has a Chance chance to drop a weapon from Table at item level Level, an ItemChance chance to drop a medkit or ammo pack, and a PartChance chance to drop a weapon part.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.LootCatalog
files.Summary: Every loot definition, loaded from content/defs/loot/*.json and checked: rarities, manufacturers, archetypes, parts, affixes, relics and loot tables. Rolls weapons from it with .

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Parts.PartFitSystem
files.Summary: Handles fitting weapon parts, anywhere and at any time (). A part from the pack goes onto one of the two weapons, replacing the part in that slot, and the replaced part goes into the pack in its place.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Rolling.RolledAffix
files.Summary: An affix on a rolled weapon, plus the values rolled for each of its ranges.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Rolling.RolledModifier
files.Summary: One rolled stat change: either flat points added, or a multiplier when Multiply is true.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Rolling.RolledPart
files.Summary: A part on a rolled weapon, plus the values rolled for each of its ranges.

files.Title: LastFleet.Loot.Rolling.RolledWeapon
files.Summary: A weapon produced by a loot roll: where it came from, what it's made of, its name, and the the simulation fires it with. The same (seed, table, level) always rolls the same weapon.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.FleetAsk
files.Summary: A fleet request that has reached the host, with the name of the lobby member who sent it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.FleetRequest
files.Summary: A joined player's request to the host about the shared fleet.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.FleetRequestKind
files.Summary: What a joined player asks the host to do with the fleet. Everything at home is shared, so anyone in the lobby can ask; the host checks the request against its fleet and carries it out.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.FleetWire
files.Summary: Packs the host's fleet for joined players, and unpacks it on their side. The fleet goes whole, as its JSON compressed with Brotli: it changes a few times between missions, never during one, so there's nothing to gain from sending only what changed. Keeping to the save's shape means a new field on the fleet needs no network code.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.LobbyClient
files.Summary: A client in a host's lobby. It joins the lobby (checking the version), keeps track of who's there and which mission is set up, and tells the host when this player is ready. When the host starts a mission, it gives the game a to use for the mission's . The connection stays open between missions.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.LobbyClientState
files.Summary: The current state of a .

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.LobbyEvent
files.Summary: Something that happened in the lobby we joined, for the game to act on.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.LobbyEventKind
files.Summary: The kind of .

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.LobbyHost
files.Summary: The host's lobby, where the squad gathers between missions. On its own it only holds the host. Once it's opened on a connection with , friends can join, mark themselves ready, and see the mission the host has set up and what everyone is carrying.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.LobbyMember
files.Summary: A player in a lobby, either the host (slot 0) or a client.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.LobbyWeapon
files.Summary: A weapon a lobby member is taking into the next mission. Holds its name and rarity rank, which picks its color.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.RelayTransport
files.Summary: Wraps the lobby's connection for one mission. The mission's or talks to this as if it were the real connection, while the lobby keeps the real one open between missions.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Prediction.PlayerPrediction
files.Summary: Client-side prediction for your own player. It runs your commands immediately through the same movement, mantle, loadout and weapon code the host runs, against the level's collision, so moving, turning and firing never wait for the host.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Prediction.PredictedHits
files.Summary: Resolves your own shots on this machine the moment they're fired, against the level's collision and against the other characters and the horde where they're drawn. A hit on an enemy shows a hit marker right away, a full round trip before the host confirms it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Protocol.HelloMessage
files.Summary: Client to host: the first message after connecting.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Protocol.InputMessage
files.Summary: Client to host: the commands for the client's latest ticks, newest first. Each command has a sequence number, one per client tick. The host applies them in order, each one once.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Protocol.MessageType
files.Summary: The first byte of every message.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Protocol.NetProtocol
files.Summary: Protocol constants.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Protocol.RejectMessage
files.Summary: Host to client: the client was refused.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Protocol.RejectReason
files.Summary: Why a host refused a client.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Protocol.WelcomeMessage
files.Summary: Host to client: the client was accepted.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.CharacterKind
files.Summary: What kind of character a snapshot entry is.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.CharacterView
files.Summary: What one client is told about where each character is, kept on the host.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.EventBuffer
files.Summary: Events received from the host, kept until the presentation processes them.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.EventCodec
files.Summary: Encodes shots and hits for the wire. They're packed down to just what a client needs to draw and play them, about a fifth of their size in memory.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.ReplicaWorld
files.Summary: A client's copy of the host's world, built from snapshots. It has the same entities, with the host's ids, and the components the presentation reads (characters, grenades, pickups, dropped weapons, targets).

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.SnapshotDelta
files.Summary: Delta compression for snapshots. Each snapshot is sent as a delta from one the client has acknowledged. Its bytes are XORed with the baseline's, so anything unchanged becomes zero, and the result is sent as runs: a count of unchanged bytes, then a count of changed bytes followed by those bytes, and so on.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.SnapshotHistory
files.Summary: The last few snapshots sent to one client (on the host) or received by it (on the client), stored by tick. These are the baselines a delta can be encoded against and decoded from.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.SnapshotWriter
files.Summary: Writes the host's world as a snapshot for one client: every character's pose and visible state, the client's own player in full (movement, weapons, loadout, grenades), grenades, pickups, dropped weapons, broken props, practice targets, and the horde near the client ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.SwarmView
files.Summary: What one client knows about the horde, kept on the host, and the horde's part of that client's snapshots. It stays within the design's budget (64 kbps for everything) no matter how many swarmlings there are.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Replication.TickEvents
files.Summary: One tick's events, in the form the presentation needs: shots (tracers, muzzle flashes), hits (markers, impacts, damage indicators), explosions, broken props, barks, and effect sounds and flashes. On the host these come from the simulation's logs. On a client they're what the host sent.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Serialization.NetReader
files.Summary: Reads what a wrote. Reading past the end throws , so a malformed message is an error the caller can handle, never a crash.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Serialization.NetWriter
files.Summary: Writes a message into a reusable buffer: little-endian numbers, variable-length integers, short strings and raw unmanaged structs. Doesn't allocate once the buffer has grown to its working size.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Serialization.Quantize
files.Summary: Packs values down small for the wire: positions snap to a grid, and directions are encoded on an octahedron.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Session.ArrivalJitter
files.Summary: Measures how unevenly a client's commands reach the host, and from that how many commands should be kept waiting there. This is the jitter buffer.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Session.ClientState
files.Summary: How far along a client is in joining a host.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Session.InputBuffer
files.Summary: One client's commands on the host, stored by sequence number. Each command is applied once, in order, one per host tick.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Session.NetClient
files.Summary: The client side of co-op. Joins a host, sends a command every tick (plus the previous few, in case packets get lost), and builds a and the host's events from what comes back.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Session.NetHost
files.Summary: The host side of co-op. Accepts clients (checking their version), spawns a player for each one, applies their commands to their players every tick, and sends them snapshots of the world and the tick's events.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Session.RemotePlayer
files.Summary: A client playing on this host.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Transport.ConditionedTransport
files.Summary: Wraps a real transport in a simulated bad network, for testing co-op over a LAN as if it were over the internet (--net-sim). Every message in either direction is delayed by the latency plus up to the jitter, and unreliable messages this machine sends are dropped at the given rate.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Transport.Delivery
files.Summary: How a message travels.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Transport.ITransport
files.Summary: Moves messages between a host and its clients. The game only talks to this interface, so the transport can be RakNet (direct IP, for playtests), an in-memory network (tests, soak runs), or Steam networking later, without changing anything above it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Transport.LinkConditions
files.Summary: Conditions on a simulated link, applied in each direction.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Transport.LoopbackNetwork
files.Summary: An in-memory network for tests and soak runs. Runs one host and any number of clients in one process, with latency, jitter and loss simulated deterministically from a seed and a clock the caller controls.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Transport.LoopbackTransport
files.Summary: One end of a .

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Transport.NetEvent
files.Summary: One transport event. For , the message is the first bytes of the buffer passed to Poll.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Transport.NetEventKind
files.Summary: The kind of event that happened on a transport.

files.Title: LastFleet.Networking.Transport.RakNetTransport
files.Summary: A transport using RakNet over UDP, from BRUTAL, for direct IP connections. The host listens on a port (forward it, or use a VPN such as Tailscale), and clients connect to its address.

files.Title: LastFleet.Physics.DebrisFragment
files.Summary: One piece of a broken prop.

files.Title: LastFleet.Physics.DebrisWorld
files.Summary: Cosmetic debris. When a prop breaks, it bursts into box fragments that tumble and bounce off the level and each other under Jolt rigid-body physics, then disappear.

files.Title: LastFleet.Physics.JoltWorld
files.Summary: The level's collision. Uses Jolt for characters moving through static geometry, and a triangle hierarchy for rays.

files.Title: LastFleet.Physics.TriangleRaycaster
files.Summary: Casts rays against a static triangle mesh using a bounding-volume hierarchy. Exact, deterministic, and doesn't allocate per query.

files.Title: LastFleet.Platform.GameWindow
files.Summary: The game window and its input state. It's a GLFW window with no graphics API attached, since Vulkan draws to it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Platform.GlfwRuntime
files.Summary: Owns GLFW's process-wide lifetime. Create one before any window and dispose it after the last window is gone.

files.Title: LastFleet.Platform.InputState
files.Summary: Keyboard and mouse state collected from GLFW callbacks. Doesn't allocate after construction.

files.Title: LastFleet.Platform.WindowMode
files.Summary: How the game window is shown on its display.

files.Title: LastFleet.Platform.WindowSettings
files.Summary: Size and title of a new window.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Data.KindNames
files.Summary: The names the procgen data gives kinds of things (a hall's structure, floor and accents, a shape's kind): each name in camel case (columns, columnFaces, l), read back whatever its case.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Data.ProcGenData
files.Summary: The designer data levels are generated from, read from content/defs/procgen: the content's tags (), surface styles (), room archetypes (), the props () and rules that place them (), the networks that join a level's things (), where its loot goes (), how its rooms are typed (), and the plans structure-first levels are built from () with the rooms of their districts ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.GeneratedLevel
files.Summary: A generated level: one mesh, its fight, its mission, its lights, the layout it came from, and which room each part of the mesh belongs to (, in part order).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Hub.HubLayout
files.Summary: The ship's hub as loaded by : the deck's mesh, where the squad comes in, and where each station is used from.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Hub.HubLevel
files.Summary: The hub between missions: the hangar deck of the fleet's ship, open to space along one side behind its shield. The squad's dropship sits on its pad. Along the walls are the mission console (pick and launch the next mission), the needs board (what the fleet has and what it's short of), the armory bench (weapons, parts, the pack) and the star map table. It's a hand-built level made in Blender (content/modules/hub/hangar_deck.gltf, docs/blender/hub.md), so it's the same on every machine.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Hub.HubStation
files.Summary: What a station on the hub's deck is for.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Hub.HubStationRule
files.Summary: One of the ship's stations as data (content/defs/hub.json): which screen it opens, which markers in the hub's model stand for it, what its prompt says, and whether the deck must have one.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Hub.HubStations
files.Summary: The ship's stations as data (content/defs/hub.json, edited in Studio's Missions mode under Ship's hub): for each screen, the markers in the hub's model that stand for it and the prompt shown there. A new place to use a screen from is a marker in Blender and its name here; what each screen does is code.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.Doorway
files.Summary: An open (or locked) passage between two placed rooms, through their matching connectors.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.Grid
files.Summary: The module grid: 4 m cells, sides and quarter turns.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.GridDoor
files.Summary: A doorway in level grid terms: its center in half cells, the side it faces out of, and its story.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.HullEdge
files.Summary: A side of a layout cell that faces out of the hull (a plan's level, ): past it is space, which a window there looks out on.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.LayoutSolver
files.Summary: Places a mission graph's rooms on the grid, then adds loops and one-way shortcuts.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.LevelLayout
files.Summary: The result of pass 2 (design doc): the mission's rooms placed on the grid, joined by doorways, with loops.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.LinearityReport
files.Summary: How linear a level is, so the designer can compare it with its recipe ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.PlacedRoom
files.Summary: A module placed in a level.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.Placement
files.Summary: A module placed in a level. It's rotated by quarter turns, the rotated footprint's corner is at cell (X, Z), and its ground floor is on story .

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.Plug
files.Summary: An unused connector that gets walled up.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.RoomTags
files.Summary: Works out the tags the generator gives each placed room (): what the room is for (role.) and where it is in the layout. That covers its deck (deck.), whether it's one of the kit's own mission rooms (type.kit), and whether it's on the mission's main path, a dead end, or on a loop. A built room also gets the content tags its archetype gave it, and a boarding action's rooms what the warship has there (mission.battery, mission.reactor, mission.suppression).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.Side
files.Summary: A side of a room module's footprint. North is -Z (the direction yaw 0 faces).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.LevelGenerator
files.Summary: Generates a level from a seed (design doc, "Procedural level generation"). Pass 1 builds the mission graph from the template, pass 2 lays out the biome's room modules, and pass 3 assembles the mesh and places the fight. The same seed, template and library always give the same level on every machine, so co-op peers only send the seed.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Airlocks.Airlock
files.Summary: Builds the airlock into the insertion bay: a chamber around the player spawns against the bay's wall that has no doorway (the hull), the outer hatch in that wall where the dropship is docked, and an inner wall with a door the mission opens once the lock has cycled ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Airlocks.AirlockLayout
files.Summary: The airlock the squad starts in, built into the insertion bay against its outer wall. The dropship is docked at the hatch in that wall, and an inner door (the level part ) opens once the lock has cycled.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Airlocks.Dropship
files.Summary: The dropship landed in a hangar, for a level boarded by its hangar rather than an airlock (docs/plans/structure- first.md, Phase 4). The squad starts in its hold, behind its rear hatch, which the mission opens once everyone is aboard and the ramp is down, just as an airlock's inner door. Its intake and cargo chute are on its hull, so tanks are hosed to it and cargo loaded into it where it stands. It's built of boxes along the hangar's length, its tail toward the hangar's doors. A mission that leaves by a hangar gets one landed there too, its hatch open, the squad taken off from its hold.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.CornerChamfer
files.Summary: A room corner cut at 45° (). It applies to a corner of the outline where the room is on one side only and neither of the two walls meeting there has a doorway. The cut runs meters along each wall from where their inner faces meet. It's built as a solid wedge in the corner: a box rotated 45°, since that's the only solid level collision supports besides an axis-aligned box. Its face is the cut and the rest sits inside the walls. Anything that runs along the walls (trims, a duct, lockers) stops short of it ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Decks
files.Summary: A station's decks. Each deck is a zone behind a keycard gate (a room's region). Gives each deck's name and color, which its room baseboards, gate bulkheads and signs, and the HUD use, so you always know which deck you're on and which one you're heading into.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.BandCrossing
files.Summary: Where a smooth hall (: a ring's bend, a bridge on the slant) goes through a doorway between two of its stretches, as a bulkhead crosses it: the stretch of the doorway's grid line inside the hall, which is wider than a doorway where the hall runs on a slant, and the hall's middle and direction there. A door there stands square across the hall, from wall to wall (), not along the grid.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.BulkheadDoor
files.Summary: A door through a bulkhead, between two compartments (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 8): a pressure door where a corridor crosses it. It stands open until one of its compartments seals, when it shuts until both are unsealed. (A service way's hatch through a bulkhead stays open: it's the way round.) A gate (a locked door, ) on a bulkhead seals the same way: its part is too.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.DoorKind
files.Summary: What kind of door a shut door is, which sets how it looks. Each kind is recognizable from across a room.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.DoorLayout
files.Summary: A door in a doorway. While shut it's a solid slab the full width, height and thickness of the doorway (its part, ). Once it opens, its two leaves slide apart into the walls (drawn by the client, ).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.DoorPlate
