files.Summary: A piece of a door's face: a plate on one of its leaves, from to along the door from its middle, to up from the floor, standing off the slab.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.GateDressing
files.Summary: The markings on each side of a gate between two decks (a locked doorway between regions): a bulkhead frame around the doorway (hazard-striped posts and a header in the color of the deck beyond), a sign beside it with that deck's number, and a band of that color across the floor in front of it. That way a gate is recognizable from across the room as the way into another part of the station, and its colors tell you which part.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.KeyCard
files.Summary: A keycard lying in the level, opening the lock with the same id.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.LockedDoor
files.Summary: A locked door: a level part () that fills a doorway until it opens. It opens with its keycard, or when the hack finishes for the gate into the last zone (), or, for a one-way shortcut, when someone stands at it on the side it opens from. is that spot: on the floor in front of the door, at half the wall's height.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.Openings
files.Summary: Handles doorway openings in the level. Where two modules' openings meet, the passage is the stretch both are open over. Whatever one opening has beyond the other (for example a wide hall's end against a kit room's 2 m doorway) is walled up in that module's own wall. An unused doorway is walled up all the way across.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.RoomDoorSpot
files.Summary: A room's own door in a plan's level: on a doorway from a room onto a hall (or into another room) that isn't a gate, a pressure door or a spawn closet's. It's or , as the room's archetype says (), and a breach in the room seals it (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.StationDoors
files.Summary: How the station's doors are built and how they look. Each is a dark slab filling the doorway, with both faces plated as two leaves in the paint for the door's kind (). A lamp above it is red (amber for the lockdown) and turns green once it's open, and a gate's post gets a keycard reader or release panel. The client slides the same plates apart as it opens. The top of the slab above the leaves stays as a transom, like a doorway's lintel.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing.DeckThemes
files.Summary: Picks which theme each deck of a level gets, from the level seed. Two decks in a row never get the same theme, as long as there are at least two to pick from.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing.HullWindowSpot
files.Summary: A window onto space in a plan's level (), as the mission's breaches need it (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10): its parts' names, where its pane is, which compartment it lets space into, and whether that compartment may ever be lost.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing.SpawnCloset
files.Summary: A spawn closet: a sealed room behind a door part () where reinforcements spawn out of sight.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing.StationDressing
files.Summary: Dresses the placed rooms so they look like a space station instead of boxes under the sky: a ceiling over every room (where no room is above it), light panels in the ceiling, and the lights they cast, colored by the room's role. A few panels are dead and a few flicker.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Hull.HullBreach
files.Summary: A weak spot in the station's outer hull, either in a wall with nothing behind it or in a roof. It's a patched plate () over a ragged hole into the dark. The horde blows it open and pours in through it.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Hull.HullBreaches
files.Summary: Builds the station's hull breaches (): weak spots in the outer hull, a few in walls with nothing behind them and a few in roofs, spread through the station with at most one per room. Each is a patched plate (its own part, ) sitting a few centimeters off the wall or ceiling over a ragged black hole (, render only). When the plate is blown away, the hole shows.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Hull.HullLook
files.Summary: How a plan's outside looks (): its plating, set in a plan's skin (plans.json).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.LevelAssembler
files.Summary: Pass 3 (design doc): turns the placed modules into one level mesh (with unused doorways walled up and locked doors in place) and populates it. That means player spawns from the insertion, soldier squads from the rooms' spawn points within the template's soldier budget, weapons, the objective and extraction. After that come the props the placement rules put in the rooms (): keycards, ammo crates, containers, cargo, supplies and tanks.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Lights.AlarmLight
files.Summary: A station alarm beacon over a doorway (). It's dark while the station is calm. Once the station goes on alert it turns amber, then red, and lights its room in that color.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Lights.LevelLight
files.Summary: A light placed in a generated level. It only lights the inside of its own room, so light never leaks through a wall (there are no shadows to block it). It's either a point light or a rect light (a panel's glass, a hall's channel, a strip). A rect light shines toward the side the cross product of its half axes points to.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Lights.LightReach
files.Summary: Works out how far a light's box reaches. It covers the light's room, and through every opening wider than a door (an open hall end, where two halls continue as one) it also covers the part of the next room straight beyond it, as wide as the opening. That way the light carries across the line between them like it naturally would. The walls on either side of the opening still block it, since the box only grows by the opening's own width. Door-width openings are left alone; light gets through those the way the bounce light does.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Lights.StationAlarms
files.Summary: Builds the station's alarm beacons (). Each room gets a housing over a doorway on the inside (big rooms get a second one over another doorway, spawn closets get none; a seam between two stretches of a hall has no wall over it, so none goes there). A stretch of smooth hall () has no wall on its cells' edges, so its beacons go on its own walls instead, clear of its doorways. The lamp is dark red glass until the station goes on alert.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.MissionLayout
files.Summary: The mission's key points in a generated level: where the team arrives, the keys and locks, the objective, the extraction point, the spawn closets, and fallback reinforcement spawns (just inside the arena's doorways, facing in) for layouts with no closet by the arena. Also the weapons and supplies lying around, the containers to search, the cargo to carry out, the tanks to pump into the dropship, and the hull breaches the horde can come through.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.PartRooms
files.Summary: The room a level part belongs to, or the two rooms a doorway's part (a lintel, a locked door) sits between, so the client can skip drawing parts of rooms it cannot see. -1 for none: such a part is always drawn.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.PatrolRoom
files.Summary: A room patrols can come out of when no spawn closet will do (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 14): one the recipe's threat names a source (a security office, crew quarters), with the spots soldiers start from in it.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Pods.EscapePods
files.Summary: Builds a pod bay's escape pods (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 4): each a capsule against the bay's hull wall, in the band the room kept clear for it (, the pods tag and its pod markers), with an open hatch the mission shuts when it launches.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Pods.PodLayout
files.Summary: An escape pod: its hatch's part, the middle of its floor, and how many it seats.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.RoomRects
files.Summary: Splits a placed room's ground story into rectangles of whole cells that cover it exactly once. A rectangular room is just its own bounds; an L becomes two. Anything laid out on a grid across a room (ceiling panels, the ceiling body) is laid out on each rectangle.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.CargoSpot
files.Summary: A cargo crate in the level that players carry out to the fleet. Its contents and amount are rolled from Table when the fight is set up. If the station was chosen for what it holds, most crates hold that.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.ContainerSpot
files.Summary: A closed container to search. Either a footlocker on the floor (its body is part of the level, so it's solid) or a case on a desk or shelf. The contents are rolled from Table when the fight is set up.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.LootSpot
files.Summary: A weapon lying in the level: rolled from loot table Table at item level Level.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.StationReservoirs
files.Summary: Deep reservoirs (the template's ). A reservoir is a big tank in a room further from the airlock's port than a hose reaches, plus an outlet on a wall near the airlock. The two are joined by the reservoir feed (, a network routed along the walls and ceilings), with one valve at the reservoir and some along the way (). In game terms it's a at the outlet: players take the hose there once every valve is open, and the gauge there shows the reservoir's level. Reservoirs are placed after everything else in the level (tanks, containers, cargo), using their own random stream, so they don't change anything else a seed produces. The reservoir, outlet and valves use the template's models ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.StationTanks
files.Summary: The station's supply tanks (). The models for the template's tank kinds (, ) are baked into the level mesh where the tank rule places them (). Each one is no further from the airlock's port, walking distance for the squad, than the template's hose reaches. Each starts as full as the template says (some are empty), and its gauge, at the model's Gauge and Gauge_Top markers, shows how full it is. The walk from the port and the spots against walls are used for the reservoir too.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.SupplySpot
files.Summary: A pile lying in the level, rolled from item table Table (content/defs/loot/items.json) when the fight is set up: a medkit, an ammo pack, a weapon part, a few of a supply...

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.TankSpot
files.Summary: A storage tank of fuel or water in the level (its model is baked into the level mesh) that the squad empties into the docked dropship. Its hose runs back through the station to the airlock's port and gets pumped while the ship is docked.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.ValveSpot
files.Summary: A valve on a reservoir's pipe (): its wheel, and where a player stands to turn it.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.WallRun
files.Summary: A straight stretch of a placed room's walls on its ground story, used by the dressing to run things along it (trims, ducts, pipes). Holds which way it faces out of the room, where it runs (in meters, along X for a north or south wall, along Z for an east or west one), where its inner face is on the cross axis, and which way is into the room (+1 or -1).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Warship.SuppressionPanels
files.Summary: A boarding action's fire suppression panels (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): one on the wall beside a doorway of each room that can burn, inside it, its model . Holding Interact at it floods the room while it burns.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Warship.WarshipFixture
files.Summary: One of a boarding action's warship fittings (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): a gun battery, its reactor, or a room's fire suppression panel.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Warship.WarshipLayout
files.Summary: What a boarding action's warship has aboard (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): its gun batteries, its reactor and its fire suppression controls. The level's rules stand them in the rooms the mission gave them (mission.battery, mission.reactor, mission.suppression: a gun deck each, an engine or reactor room, damage control).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Looting.CacheLoot
files.Summary: A cache of weapons in each room.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Looting.ItemTables
files.Summary: The item tables a room's piles, footlockers, cases and cargo are rolled from.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Looting.LootAssignment
files.Summary: The loot that rooms matching a tag query get (loot.json): a cache of weapons, a chance at their deck's stashes, the tables their piles, containers and cargo are rolled from, and item levels added to what's rolled there.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Looting.LootData
files.Summary: Where a level's loot goes (loot.json): the tag-based assignments () in order, plus how many stashes each deck gets when the template's even split won't do. Without a loot.json, the built-in assignments () put loot where the mission template always has.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Looting.LootKind
files.Summary: The kinds of loot in a level, used to say which kind an assignment's item levels apply to ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Looting.LootTables
files.Summary: Item tables, by what's rolled from them. A null table means the mission template's table is used.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Looting.RoomLoot
files.Summary: The loot a room gets, with its assignments resolved against the mission template (): its cache, its stash weight and table, the tables its piles, containers and cargo are rolled from, and the item levels added to each.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Looting.StashLoot
files.Summary: How likely a room is to hold one of its deck's stashes. The Director hides stashes where they reward going out of the way, so the weight goes up for each room deeper off the main path than the first, and for each soldier guarding the room.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.AirlockModels
files.Summary: The models of the airlock's fittings in the hull (a mission template's "airlock"): the dropship's intake, where a tank's hose couples, and its cargo chute, each a station prop ("file/Object").

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.AlertSettings
files.Summary: How a mission's station alert level builds up (its template's "alert"): how it rises over time and with noise, how little it drops, and what it does to patrols and the horde. The fight's Director reads these (see its AlertTuning).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.BoardingTargets
files.Summary: Where a boarding action's targets are in a ship (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): its gun batteries, its reactor and its fire suppression controls. Read the same from the level on every machine, so the host's mission and everyone's markers agree.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.BreachRule
files.Summary: How a plan mission's breaches go (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10; the breaches block of a template's plan): the chance a breach seals its compartment for good when the mission can still be finished without it, and the districts never lost, whose compartments only ever seal for a while. How tough windows are, the pull and the timers are every mission's (breaches.json).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.EarlyExtractionSettings
files.Summary: Settings for leaving early on the docked dropship (a mission template's "earlyExtraction"): whether the squad can, how long they hold at the airlock to leave, and what the fleet needs to get for it to count as a success. That requisition is the supplies running short, topped up to ReserveJumps jumps of reserve, with some minimum amount either way.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.ExitRule
files.Summary: How a plan mission's squad gets on or off: the kinds of exit it would rather use, in order. The first kind the level has wins.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.FleetRule
files.Summary: The fleet seen from a plan's windows (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10): how many ships hang in space round the level, and how far off, set in the mission template's plan (fleet).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.GenerationSettings
files.Summary: The settings a lobby can change on a mission template before a level is generated: how many decks, how many soldiers, how much loot, how many stories, and how many rooms are built from the seed. They're encoded in the level's name (), so every co-op peer generates the same level from the name alone.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.KeycardRule
files.Summary: Where a plan mission's keycards go: one for each gate the hack doesn't open, in a room of the zone before its gate, off the way through.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.KeycardStep
files.Summary: The keycard for each deck's gate into the next (but the gate the hack opens), on a branch off the deck's way through, sometimes behind a room to explore: before its lock, so the level can always be finished. On every deck.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.LevelRecipe
files.Summary: How a level's mission graph is grown, deck by deck (). It's a list of steps in order: first the main path (), then the keycard (), then any side and loot rooms. Every step is applied to each deck in turn, so the level is always finishable by construction: each keycard sits on its deck before the gate it opens. This is a mission template's recipe. A template without one grows from its room counts ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.LoopRules
files.Summary: How a level's loops get made, beyond how many each zone gets (). Sets how far apart in the room tree a loop's two ends have to be, how long a corridor routed around corners for a loop can be, what fraction of rooms should end up on a loop, the most that should be dead ends, and how many one-way shortcuts cross each gate between zones. Loops keep getting added until both the loop and dead-end targets are met, or no more fit.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.LootRoomsStep
files.Summary: Loot rooms, each off any room of the deck but its ends (and other loot rooms).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.LootSettings
files.Summary: Weapon loot settings for a mission's level (design doc, "Procedural weapons and loot"). Loot tables are only named here, not loaded; the game rolls them. Item level goes up by one per zone, so deeper decks have better weapons. Loot rooms hold caches. On top of that, the Director hides a few stashes in each zone, placed to reward going out of the way or taking on a guarded room.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.MainPathStep
files.Summary: Builds the main path through each deck: the first room (the insertion, or a transit set piece behind the gate), some rooms along the way, then the objective and arena on the second-to-last deck and extraction at the end of the last. It's always the recipe's first step and runs on every deck.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.MissionGraph
files.Summary: Pass 1 (design doc): the mission as a tree of rooms starting from the insertion, with key and lock pairs. It's grown by the template's recipe (), applying each step in turn on each deck, so it's always completable by construction: each keycard sits off the path before its lock.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.MissionNode
files.Summary: A room in the mission graph.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.MissionTemplate
files.Summary: A mission template (design doc, "Mission types" and "Pass 1: mission graph"), read from content/defs/missions/*.json. It sets how many rooms of each kind, how many key and lock pairs, loops and soldiers, and how many stories the level can climb through (1 keeps it flat).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.ObjectiveRule
files.Summary: What a plan mission's squad comes for and where it is: a room of the zone before the last (docs/plans/structure- first.md, "Objective kinds"). Whatever its kind, finishing it opens the gate into the last zone, where extraction is.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.PlanChoice
files.Summary: A plan a mission can be laid out by (plans.json), and how often it's picked against the mission's others.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.PlanRecipe
files.Summary: How a mission reads itself into a plan's level (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "The mission recipe"). The level's structure is built first, so there's nothing to grow: these are rules for choosing among the rooms it has.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.PodRule
files.Summary: A plan mission's escape pods: bays on the hull, each with a pod or two, that take one or two players off at any time (never a crate). Whoever gets off by whatever way, the squad ends up together.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.RecipeStep
files.Summary: One step of a level's recipe (): what it adds to each deck's rooms, in the recipe's order.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.RecipeStepKind
files.Summary: The kinds of recipe step, as named in a template's recipe ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.ReservoirSettings
files.Summary: Settings for deep reservoirs of fuel or water (a mission template's "reservoir"). A reservoir is a big tank deeper in the station than a hose can reach. It's piped back to an outlet near the airlock through valves the squad has to open (one at the reservoir and some along the way) before the hose can be run from the outlet to the dropship.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.RoomRole
files.Summary: What a room is for in a mission.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.RoomRule
files.Summary: Which of a plan's rooms a mission rule is after: those with any of 's tags, from their archetype (archetypes.json), a tag also matching every tag under it (room.storage takes room.storage.armory). With no tags, every room.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.SideRoomsStep
files.Summary: Adds side rooms to explore. Each is a dead end off the deck's main path, sometimes two rooms deep. A one-deck level gets none.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.StationSupplies
files.Summary: The supplies a station's cargo can hold, as defined in the game's data (the loot data's fleet supplies, put into use with ; with no data, ). Lists every supply a station can be chosen for (a ), each with its color, used for a tank's band and glow when it holds that supply. Which ones are kept in tanks is up to the mission template (). Every co-op peer generates its levels from the same set.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.TankKind
files.Summary: A kind of supply tank a station's rooms can have (a mission template's "tankKinds"). It sets the model (a station prop in content/props, ), how much room it takes, which supplies it can hold, and how often it's picked over other kinds that can hold the same supply.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.ThreatRule
files.Summary: How hard a plan mission's places are defended, and what that sets (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "Threat drives the fight"; the threat block of a template's plan). Each zone's threat rises from the first to the last, scaled by its district and by what a room is (a security office more, quarters less). While the squad is somewhere, its threat sets how often the Director sends a patrol and how big; the station's alert speeds both on top. Patrols come from the spawn closets beside rooms or on a service way first.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.AngledHall
files.Summary: Builds a stretch of ring hall smooth (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 7): its cells are still the grid's, but its walls follow its band (: round a ring's bend, or straight on a slant) as straight sides, each a box turned to its side, so the hall reads as a curve instead of steps. The rooms either side keep their walls on the grid.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.GltfNodes
files.Summary: Reads the node tree of a .gltf or .glb file: names, transforms and custom properties, but not geometry.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.HallArc
files.Summary: A hall bent round a center: a ring hall's corridor (), the band either side of a circle out from .

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.HallBand
files.Summary: The floor plan of a hall built smooth rather than stepped on the grid (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 7): a band either side of a middle line, on the ground (X and Z, in meters). A ring hall's middle line is a circle (), a bridge's on a slant a straight line (). Its walls are the band's edges cut into straight sides no longer than .

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.HallLine
files.Summary: A straight hall on a slant: a bridge running out from a ring station's core at any angle (), the band either side of the line from to , open at both ends.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.HallTheme
files.Summary: A deck theme and how its halls are laid out (): width and length, how often they're two stories tall, how open they are, and the surface style that sets how they look. A mission template lists its themes (, "hallThemes" in its file). If it doesn't, is used.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.KitRooms
files.Summary: A biome's kit of rooms (): the archetypes offered to every level in the biome. Each one is built once, seeded from its own id, so the kit is identical in every level and on every machine, just like the hand-made modules it replaced. Each becomes a module with its archetype's id and fills that archetype's roles: the insertion bay, the corridors and stairwell, the spawn closet, the keycard room, the objective and extraction rooms, and the rooms in between.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.ModuleConnector
files.Summary: A doorway on a module's footprint, at the middle of cell along , on story of the module (0 for the ground floor, 1 for one story up). The opening is wide and centered along the side from the cell's middle. That covers both a standard 2 m kit doorway and a wide hall's fully open end. Where two openings of different widths meet, the level walls up whatever part doesn't face the other opening (LevelAssembler).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.ModuleLibrary
files.Summary: A biome's room modules (its kit, , plus the level's own), sorted by id so the order is stable.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.ModuleLight
files.Summary: An extra light that comes with a module, on top of the ceiling panels (for example a glow under a floor grate or along a trim strip), in module coordinates. Like the panel lights, it only lights its own room. If it has half axes it's a rect light: the glowing surface itself, shining toward the side the cross product of its axes points to (PointLight.Rect).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.ModuleReader
files.Summary: Turns a room's scene, as written by a built room or hall (, ), into a . It also checks the scene against the kit's rules, so a mistake is reported by name when the room is built instead of showing up as a broken level.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.ParametricHall
files.Summary: Procedurally built halls for a deck's theme () in its surface style (). The theme sets the size and openness: one to three cells wide, two to four long, one or two stories, and open across a wide end so two halls placed end to end read as one. The style sets the look (): ribs, arches, columns or pillars along the hall; a floor of plain plate, a grated channel lit from below, or light strips along the walls and down the middle; and lighting along the bottom or top of the walls or on whatever stands along the hall (the lighting is in ParametricHall.Lights.cs).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.ParametricRoom
files.Summary: Procedurally built rooms, as opposed to hand-made ones: a footprint of any size and shape (a rectangle, or an L, a U, or a cross from a shape recipe), doorways on every side, and furniture laid out in one of a few styles (offices, a warehouse, a lab, a plaza), all from a seed. Each one is built the same way a hand-made module would be, from boxes and markers, and read by . That way it follows the kit's rules (whole cells, clear doorways) and gets spawn spots found from its geometry the same way.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.RoomFinish
files.Summary: The finishing details of a built room () beyond its footprint: its surface style, its furnishing, how much its corners are cut, and whether pillars hold up its ceiling.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.RoomModule
files.Summary: A room that levels are laid out from. It's either built from an archetype () or a hall, and checked against the kit's rules by . It holds the geometry, the footprint in grid cells, the connectors, the roles it can fill (tags), and markers in module coordinates.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.SceneNode
files.Summary: A node in a glTF scene: its name, world transform, whether it has a mesh, and its custom properties.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.ShipBay
files.Summary: A hangar's ship entrance (docs/plans/structure-first.md, hangars): its wall on the hull left open the room's full height, but for a post at each end, behind a field that keeps the air in and people from walking out (shots and the view go through it). A dropship comes in through it to its pad, so the lane from it in is kept clear of anything placed (). In the room's own frame.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.ILaneObstacles
files.Summary: Answers what's in the way in a level where a network lane might run: geometry, light panels, ducts and props.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaidNetwork
files.Summary: A network as laid in a level, for designers to inspect (the Studio preview): the route it took, what each section runs along, its cost, and the cheapest route it didn't take (). The alternative is only computed the first time it's asked for.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaneBlock
files.Summary: What's in the way where a lane would run ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaneEdge
files.Summary: A straight lane between two nodes of a , along one of the level's axes.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaneGraph
files.Summary: The graph of places a level's networks can run (). That covers a band along every room's walls above the doorway lintels, a higher lane along them (under the ceiling, or up a tall room's wall), a standoff lane offset from the wall to get past whatever already runs along it, straight spans across open ceilings from wall to wall, risers between these and up tall rooms' walls, crossings through walls and floors rooms share (including next to a doorway) and through doorway lintels, and the empty cells enclosed by rooms (service cells).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaneKind
files.Summary: What a lane in a runs along or through. Each kind is priced by a network's . Every lane is straight, either horizontal or vertical, along one of the level's axes.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaneNode
files.Summary: A point in a where lanes meet.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaneUsage
files.Summary: Tracks which lanes of a level's the networks have used so far, and by which kind. A lane only carries networks of one kind, side by side (each new one further out). So networks of the same kind bundle together, and a different kind finds the lane taken.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.NetworkCosts
files.Summary: What a network's route costs for each kind of lane (). Costs are integers so every machine finds the same route. They're charged per meter along a lane, once for each wall or lintel passed through, and once for each bend. A higher cost keeps routes off that kind of lane unless nothing cheaper gets there.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.NetworkLimits
files.Summary: Limits on how far a network can run in places where a pipe is most in the way.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.NetworkRoute
files.Summary: A network's path through a level's , found by : the nodes it passes in order, the edges between them, and its total cost.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.NetworkRouter
files.Summary: Finds a network's cheapest route through a level's lanes () using A*. Costs are integers () and ties are broken by node index, so every machine finds the same route.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.NetworkSpec
files.Summary: A type of network that connects things in a level (a fuel feed, a water main, a cable run). It defines what the route costs for each kind of lane, how far it can cross open ceiling or run through empty cells, and what its pipe looks like. Loaded from networks.json ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.PipeLook
files.Summary: What a network's pipe looks like.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Arrangements.Arrangement
files.Summary: How a rule lays out its props as a group (the arrange field in rules.json): a row of pieces, or several rows, treated as a single spot for the rule's anchor. For example a galley's tables, a lab's benches back to back, or a dormitory's bunks.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Arrangements.ArrangementAxis
files.Summary: The direction an 's rows run in.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Arrangements.ArrangementKind
files.Summary: How an lays out its pieces.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Furniture.Attachment
files.Summary: Extra furniture placed with a piece at its model's Attach_<Group>_<n> empties (the attach field in props.json), for example chairs around a table or a stool at a counter. Each one is placed with its origin at the empty, facing the piece, either tucked in or pulled out, and rotated a little. It's placed and checked together with the piece.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Furniture.ColliderEdge
files.Summary: An edge of a collider's outline, in the placed model's space ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Furniture.ColliderReport
files.Summary: What a model is collided with, as furniture () or a station fixture (), with a given , built exactly as the generator sets it into the level, and what's worth knowing about it: Studio's Models mode shows it over the model. Headless, so it's tested like the rest of the generator.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Furniture.Furnishing
files.Summary: A furnishing style for built rooms, from the furnishings in rules.json (offices, a warehouse, and so on). It holds the rules used to place furniture while the room is built. A room archetype names the furnishing it uses; a room without one picks one at random.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Furniture.FurnitureLoot
files.Summary: A socket group on a placed piece that a designer gave loot to (), with the positions of its reachable sockets. Positions are in room space while the room is built, and in level space after. Which sockets get filled, and with what, is rolled with the level ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Furniture.FurnitureModel
files.Summary: A furniture model (a top-level object in a file under content/props, named by its prop's model), as the generator builds it into a room: its footprint, its solid boxes, its visible shape, and the spots on it where items go () and where other furniture attaches (). Its origin is the center of its base, and it faces into the room along its forward axis (glTF -Z, Blender +Y), the same as a station fixture.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Furniture.FurnitureSocket
files.Summary: A marked point on a furniture model (), in model space. It's either a spot where an item sits (Socket_Top_1) or where another piece attaches (Attach_Seat_1).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Furniture.SocketLoot
files.Summary: The loot a group of sockets on a furniture model holds (the sockets field in props.json). Once a designer gives a group loot, the group belongs to them, so the placement rules don't put anything on it. Which of its sockets get filled is rolled with the level.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.MissionMarker
files.Summary: A spot the mission needs in a room. A piece of furniture can stand in for it (): when a built room's furnishing places that piece, it marks the spot where it stands, the same way a marker in a hand-made module does.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.FurniturePattern
files.Summary: A furniture pattern (a furnishing's patterns in rules.json): a small grid of half-meter cells, drawn as the room is seen from above, saying what has to be where (a wall behind, open floor in front, a desk beside) and what it places there. A room finds every spot and turn it fits, scores them, and keeps the best until it has as many as its count ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.PatternCell
files.Summary: One cell of a .

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.PatternCellKind
files.Summary: What one cell of a asks of the room, or puts in it.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.PatternFacing
files.Summary: The way one of a pattern's pieces faces, as the pattern is drawn: toward its bottom row, its top row, or either side. The pattern turns and mirrors as it's matched, and its pieces turn with it.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.PatternFit
files.Summary: Whether a pattern fits at a cell turned one way, and why not ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.PatternPiece
files.Summary: One piece a places: its prop, standing in the middle of its block of cells (and pushed back against any wall the block touches), facing the way it says.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.PatternPlacement
files.Summary: What a room's furniture patterns placed ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.PatternPreview
files.Summary: A built room as its furnishing's patterns left it, for showing a designer what their patterns do: the room, its cells, what the patterns placed, how every pattern and rule did, and why a pattern does or doesn't fit at a cell.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.PatternSymbols
files.Summary: The fixed symbols a pattern's cells are drawn with in rules.json. Letters are the pattern's own, given meaning by its key: a piece it places, or a prop that has to be there already.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.PatternTurn
files.Summary: One way a pattern can lie in a room: turned clockwise by quarter turns as seen from above (none: its top row to the north), after being mirrored left to right if .

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.RoomCellKind
files.Summary: What one half-meter cell of a room is, as patterns see it ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Patterns.RoomCells
files.Summary: A room as furniture patterns see it: its floor in half-meter cells (the cells of its , with a ring of one more around them), each a wall, a doorway, floor or the walkway between its doorways, and what stands on it so far.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.PlacementGrid
files.Summary: The grid sizes props are placed on, exposed for tools that draw them.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Props.PlacedProp
files.Summary: A prop placed by a rule, with a bounding box from to .

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Props.PropBreaks
files.Summary: What material a piece of furniture breaks as when it's shot apart. if it doesn't break.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Props.PropDefinition
files.Summary: A prop that rules place (props.json): its gameplay kind, its size, and for furniture how it's built, either as a box in its color or from its model ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Props.PropKind
files.Summary: What a prop is in gameplay terms, which decides what placing it creates. Furniture is built into the room. A footlocker, case, cargo crate, supply pile, keycard, ammo crate or tank is a mission object.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Props.WeightedProp
files.Summary: One of the props a rule can place, with how often it gets picked compared to the rule's other props.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Reach.ReachFailure
files.Summary: Why a piece couldn't be blocked out on a .

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.BuiltInPlacements
files.Summary: The props and rules the game uses when the content doesn't provide any (no props.json or rules.json). The shipped files contain the same thing, so a level comes out identical with or without them. On top of that, the files add the furnishings for the kit rooms () and their props, which only the files' archetypes use.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.PlacementAnchor
files.Summary: Where in a room a rule looks for spots to put its props.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.PlacementCount
files.Summary: How many of a rule's props a room gets. By default, with probability , the room gets between and (each count equally likely). When is set, the count scales with the room instead: a number picked between its two values, times the cells in the room's bounds, rounded.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.PlacementData
files.Summary: The props and the rules that place them: props by id (props.json), the furnishings for built rooms, and the rules that fill a level's rooms (rules.json). Each list is in the order it's applied.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.PlacementRule
files.Summary: A rule for placing props (rules.json): which props, in which rooms, where in the room, how many, and what space they have to leave clear. Rules run highest first, each one in every room it applies to.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.PlacementSkip
files.Summary: Why a spot a rule tried for a prop was rejected.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.RuleTally
files.Summary: How a rule did in one room: how many props it wanted, how many it placed, and why the spots it tried were rejected.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.ArmPart
files.Summary: A straight run of cells out from a point: a station's arm, a ring station's bridge, a docking boom. It grows from its in its direction for a length picked from its range, as wide as its width either side of its line, so it stays on its line however long it's drawn.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.BoxModule
files.Summary: A rectangle of cells: a station's hub or arm, a ship's sponson, a module bolted on. Its size is picked from its ranges; it can be mirrored across the centerline (a pair of sponsons from one part).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.BridgePart
files.Summary: A straight run out from a center at any angle: a ring station's bridge from its core to its ring, on a slant as often as not (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 7). It covers every cell its band ( cells across) touches, from 's first count of cells out from the center's middle to its second, so a hall laid on it runs smooth along its line () rather than stepped on the grid.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.CrossHall
files.Summary: A hall straight across a part, at a share of its length: a cross passage joining a ship's passageways, a hub's corridor across it. It reaches cells either side of the part's line, or as far as the envelope allows with cells to spare.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.DistrictPaint
files.Summary: Cells a designer painted with one of a plan's districts (), as rows of text the way a mask is (): # for a painted cell, anything else for none. The first row is the one with the least Z, and each row's first character the cell with the least X.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.DistrictProgram
files.Summary: What a district is made of (districts.json): its anchor, the set piece its section is built round (a mess, a cargo hold, the bridge), and the rooms that fill the rest of its plots.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.DistrictRoom
files.Summary: A kind of room a district is made of (): the archetype it's built from (its style, furnishing and tags; its shape comes from the plot it's cut from), how many cells along its hall it takes, how often it's picked, whether it comes in a row of the same, and whether it's somewhere you go into rather than through.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.Envelope
files.Summary: The outline of a level on one deck: the grid cells inside its hull, built from a plan's parts for a seed. Everything later in the structure-first pipeline (halls, sections, rooms) happens inside it, and its hull edges are where the level meets space.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.ExitPlanner
files.Summary: Finds a plan level's ways on and off (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 4): airlock vestibules, small rooms on the hull that open only onto a corridor, so the squad boards into a hallway rather than a store; and rooms on the hull for the squad to be taken off from.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.ExitPoint
files.Summary: A way on or off a plan's level: a room against the hull and the side of it the hull is on, or a hangar the dropship lands in.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.FillHall
files.Summary: A hall that is the whole of the part it's laid on: every cell of it inside the envelope, whatever its shape. A mask painted as a hallway, a box made a concourse, an arm that is all corridor.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.HallPart
files.Summary: One of a plan's halls, carved after the envelope and before any room. A hall is laid on one of the plan's parts () and follows the shape that part was drawn at (), so it fits however long or wide the part came out. Halls are carved in order; corridors first, then service ways round them.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.HallTier
files.Summary: What a hall is for, which says how wide it reads and what it joins.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.HullProfile
files.Summary: A ship's hull: a length and a beam picked from their ranges, and a profile saying how wide it is along its length. It's mirrored across its centerline, with the bow at its and the stern toward +X.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.LevelPlan
files.Summary: A kind of level, as a designer composed it in Studio from parts: a frigate, a carrier, a station of hub and spokes, a ring station. Its envelope is built from its parts in order (), each adding cells or cutting them out. Its halls are carved into the envelope next, then it's cut into sections ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.MissionEmbedder
files.Summary: Reads a mission into a plan's level before its rooms are built (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 4), by the template's recipe (). The structure is already there, so nothing is grown: the embedder picks among the rooms the level has.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PaintedMask
files.Summary: Cells a designer painted, as rows of text: # for a cell, anything else for none. The first row is the one with the least Z, and each row's first character the cell with the least X.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PartMode
files.Summary: What a plan's part does to the envelope built so far.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PartShape
files.Summary: The shape a part was drawn at for a seed, so halls and sections can follow it however long or wide it came out: a line it runs along (from its origin, in its direction, for its length, with cells either side of it), or a ring's center, radius and width.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanCore
files.Summary: A plan's stair core: stairs from one deck up to the one above, at a fixed frame of the ship, so it's in the same place on every seed. It stands as near the frame as a stairwell fits, clear of the halls on both decks, its foot joined to a corridor on the lower deck and its landing to one on the upper by short passages where they don't touch.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanDeck
files.Summary: One deck of a plan (): its name, and its sections' districts if not the plan's.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanDock
files.Summary: Where the dropship docks to take the squad off: one side of a cell of the extraction room, on the hull with no doorway in it, where the airlock's outer hatch goes.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanDoor
files.Summary: A door in a plan's structure, on one side of a cell.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanDoorKind
files.Summary: The doors a plan's structure puts in before any room: where halls cross bulkheads.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanDoorway
files.Summary: A doorway between two pieces of a plan's level, on one side of a cell of the first.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanDoorwayKind
files.Summary: What joins two pieces of a plan's level.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanLevel
files.Summary: A plan's level for a seed, built from the outside in: its structure (), then the space its halls leave cut into rooms from each section's district program, then every room's doors, then every piece built as a room module and placed on the grid.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanMission
files.Summary: The mission read into a plan's level (): each piece's zone and role, each doorway's lock, the way through, and the mission graph the rest of generation reads, in which each piece is the node of its own index.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanMissionException
files.Summary: A mission recipe can't be read into a plan's level for a seed: no room on the hull for an airlock, or too few sections for two zones. The generator tries a seed made from this one.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanPart
files.Summary: One part of a level's plan (). Each part covers some grid cells, picked from its own random stream within the ranges a designer gave, and adds them to the envelope or cuts them out of it.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanPicture
files.Summary: Draws a plan's structure from above as a picture, for checking a plan by eye outside Studio (Studio's --plan-png): its sections tinted, its halls (main corridors palest, service ways brown), its bulkheads in red, its pressure doors in yellow and hatches in orange, the hull's edges, the centerline, and a mark every five cells (20 m). The bow is to the left.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanPiece
files.Summary: One piece of a plan's level, built as one room module: a room cut from a plot, or a stretch of hall. Long halls are built in stretches at most 8 cells each way, joined by openings as wide as the hall.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanPieceKind
files.Summary: What a piece of a plan's level is: a room, a stretch of corridor or of service way, a spawn closet or stairs.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanPin
files.Summary: A set piece a designer pinned to a plan (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 11): a room of an archetype that goes here, or where the squad boards. Like a stair core (), it's placed on a part, so it follows the part however long or wide a seed draws it: along a line (a hull, a box, an arm), as a share of its length and cells off its middle line; round a ring, as cells from its center at its fewest radius, grown with it.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanPinKind
files.Summary: What a plan's pin holds in place ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanStructure
files.Summary: A plan's structure for a seed, before any room: its envelope, the halls carved into it, the sections bulkheads cut it into (each with its district), the pressure doors and hatches where halls cross bulkheads, and service stubs so every section a service way passes has a hatch onto a corridor. Also what's wrong with it, for Studio and the tests.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.ProfilePoint
files.Summary: A point on a hull's profile (): how wide the hull is at a place along it.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.RingHall
files.Summary: A hall round a ring part: a ring station's ring corridor, the corridor round its core. It runs cells in from the ring's outside, meters wide, walkable all the way round, built smooth round its bend () on every cell it touches.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.RingPart
files.Summary: A ring of cells round a center: a ring station's outer ring, or a disc when it's as wide as its radius (a hub). A cell is in it when its middle is within the outer radius and beyond the inner one, worked out in whole numbers.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.RingSplit
files.Summary: A ring part cut into sections by angle, when each part is its own section (): a bulkhead out from its center at each of , so a ring station's ring is several sections, each its own zone, rather than one. The first piece round from the first quarter keeps the part's own section; the others get sections of their own after every part's, with the part's district.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.SectionCuts
files.Summary: Bulkheads across one of a plan's parts, at shares of its length: a ship cut bow to stern into sections. Every cell of the envelope takes the section of where it falls along that part's line.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.SectionPlan
files.Summary: How a plan's envelope is cut into sections (the parts between bulkheads, which become zones), and what each one is: bulkheads across one part (), each part its own section (a station's hub, each arm, each bridge), or districts painted on the plan's cells ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.SpineHall
files.Summary: A hall along a part's line: a ship's spine, a passageway either side of it, a station arm's corridor, a bridge. It runs from to of the part's length (shares that may go past 0 and 1 to reach into the parts beside it), at cells across, and stops where the envelope ends or leaves fewer than cells either side of it for rooms. Only its longest stretch is kept, so it never breaks in two.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.Footprint
files.Summary: The grid cells a room occupies (each square and one story tall), in the room's own coordinates: X along its width, Z along its depth, and Level for its stories starting at 0. A kit module's footprint is a rectangle. A room built from a shape recipe can be any connected shape (an L, a U, a cross).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.RoomArchetype
files.Summary: A kind of room the generator builds from designer data (archetypes.json). It sets the room's shape, the content tags it carries (which placement rules match on), the mission roles it can play, the surface style it's built and dressed in, and how it's furnished. A mission template lists the archetypes its built rooms are picked from, each picked by its weight.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.ShapeBuilder
files.Summary: Makes a room's footprint from a and a random stream: a rectangle, an L, a T, a U, a cross, a blob, or a designer's stamp as drawn. The result is one story, with every cell connected to the others through shared sides, and its bounds start at cell (0, 0). The same recipe and stream give the same shape on every machine. Shapes are always generated in one orientation; the layout rotates them.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.ShapeKind
files.Summary: The kinds of shape a room's footprint can be built from ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.ShapeRecipe
files.Summary: How a room's footprint is made (): its kind, how big its bounds can be, and how much of them it leaves out. Everything is in grid cells (4 m), picked from the seed within the given ranges.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.StairKind
files.Summary: How the stairs up to a tall room's floor climb (), one story at a time. A climb of more than one story (from a floor two or more stories below, with the stories in between open) stacks them, with a landing at each story.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.StoryFloor
files.Summary: The floor of one story of a tall room, above its ground story (). Holds what kind of floor it is, how far in from the walls it reaches, and how the stairs climb to it from a floor below.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.UpperFloorKind
files.Summary: The kind of floor a story of a tall room has above its ground story ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.VerticalSpec
files.Summary: Describes a room more than one story tall (): a floor, or no floor, for each story above the ground story, from the bottom up. Each floor is reached by stairs from a floor below it (the nearest one where they fit, otherwise one further down, climbing through the open stories in between). Edges over open space get railings, and doorways go where a floor reaches the wall. A story with no floor leaves the room open through it. For example, a three-story room with no middle floor has just a ground floor and a top floor.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Seeding.GenerationStage
files.Summary: The stages of a level's generation. Each has its own random streams ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Seeding.Streams
files.Summary: The random streams a level is generated from: one per stage, one per room in a stage, and one per rule for a room. Each stream depends only on the level's seed and its own keys, never on what another stream drew. So changing one room's rules leaves every other room, and every other stage, unchanged.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.EdgeClassifier
files.Summary: Works out a room's structure from its shape: the floor and ceiling, the walls as straight runs between corners (cut open at the doorways), the doorways, and the corners. Each is a in the room's own coordinates. Surface styles build geometry from them, so no wall ever has to be placed or rotated by hand.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.FineGrid
files.Summary: One story of a room at resolution: which half-meter squares of its floor are inside the room. Shapes finer than the layout's 4 m grid (chamfered corners, insets, pillars) get carved out here, and walls, floors and ceilings are found from its edges.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.FineRect
files.Summary: A block of fine cells (), starting at (, ) and by in size.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.MarkerFrame
files.Summary: Where a piece of structure is and which way it faces: a point on its surface, the direction into the room (), and the direction along it (). Walls get built and props get placed in this frame, so nothing generated ever has to be rotated by hand.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.StructureMarker
files.Summary: A piece of a room's structure, found from the room's shape: what it is, where it is, which way it faces, and how long it is. Surface styles build geometry from markers, and placement rules anchor props to them.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.StructureMarkerKind
files.Summary: What kind of structure piece a marker is, as found from the room's shape.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.WallOpening
files.Summary: A gap in a room's wall: a doorway, or a hall's end open all across. Given as two points on the room's outline in its own coordinates (meters, X and Z), on one story; the wall runs between them are left open.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.ColorSource
files.Summary: Where a style gets its color from ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.DuctStyle
files.Summary: A duct under the ceiling along one long wall of a room (not a corridor's or a narrow room's).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.HallAccents
files.Summary: Extra lights a hall built in a style can have besides its floor light (). Flags, so any combination works. Each piece is its own light, and it's broken up wherever there's a doorway.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.HallFloor
files.Summary: The kind of floor a hall has (), and how it's lit.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.HallLook
files.Summary: How a hall built in a style looks (): what stands along it, what kind of floor it has, the floor's light, and accent lighting along the walls and on the structure. The walls and floor plate use the style's and , and the ceiling panels use the style's .

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.HallStructure
files.Summary: What stands along a hall ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.LightStyle
files.Summary: A room's ceiling light panels: whether it has any, how many are dead or flicker, and how bright they are.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.PipeStyle
files.Summary: Pipes under the ceiling along the long wall opposite the duct, one under and out from the other.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.StyleColor
files.Summary: A color in a style: either a fixed color or the room's deck or role color, multiplied by (0.5 is half as bright).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.SurfaceLook
files.Summary: How a surface looks: its color (linear RGB) and its material (an id in content/defs/materials.json).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.SurfaceStyle
files.Summary: How a room's structure is built and how it looks. The generator builds the walls, floors and the rest from the room's structure markers using its style (), and dresses it the same way (ceilings, trims, ducts, lights), so designers never have to model a wall. Styles are designer data in content/defs/procgen/styles.json. A style can inherit anything it doesn't set from another style (its base), and ultimately from .

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Styles.TrimStyle
files.Summary: A band round a room's walls on its ground story, broken at its doorways: a baseboard, a stripe.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Tags.BuiltInTags
files.Summary: The tags the generator sets itself: what a room is for in the mission (role.), where it is in the layout (layout.) and which deck it's on (deck.), and what a piece of its structure is (wall., corner.*). They're in every . Content can use them in rules but can't define them again.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Tags.TagDefinition
files.Summary: A tag designers can use in rules, with its dotted name and what it means.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Tags.TagQuery
files.Summary: Decides which tag sets a rule applies to: sets that have at least one of (if any are given), all of , and none of . Each tag matches itself and everything nested under it, so any: [room.storage] matches a room tagged room.storage.cold.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Tags.TagRegistry
files.Summary: Every tag a level's rules can use, each with its own id. Tags are dotted names that nest: room contains room.storage, which contains room.storage.cold, and a rule asking for room.storage also matches its children (, ).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Tags.TagSet
files.Summary: The tags on something (a room, a marker, a prop), all from one . A set with room.storage.cold also counts as having room.storage and room ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.AdjacencyRule
files.Summary: Two rooms the mission joins (a room and the one it is reached from), one matching A and the other B, may never be: no lab next to a lab, say.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.CountRule
files.Summary: A rule limiting how many rooms matching Where each deck, or the whole level, can have.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.CountScope
files.Summary: What a counts over.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.DistanceRule
files.Summary: A rule on how far apart rooms matching A are from rooms matching B, counted in rooms along the mission's paths. They're never closer than Min (for example two cargo holds kept well apart). If Max is set, each A room must also be within that many steps of some B room (for example a lab near the objective).

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.NodeTyping
files.Summary: Why one mission room is its type.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.RoomTyper
files.Summary: Types the rooms of a mission () before they're laid out. Each room becomes either one of the mission's archetypes or the kit's own, so the level's room mix follows the designers' rules ().

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.RoomTyping
files.Summary: The result of typing a level's mission rooms (). Each room is either one of the mission's archetypes or the kit's own (null). It also records why: what each room could have been, at what weight, and which rule ruled out each type it didn't get.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.RoomTypingException
files.Summary: Thrown when a level's rooms can't be typed under the rules (). The trace says why.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.TypingData
files.Summary: How a level's rooms get typed (typing.json): how often a room is left to the kit's own rooms instead of being built from one of the mission's archetypes, and the rules the mix has to follow (). If there's no typing.json, is used.

files.Title: LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.TypingRule
files.Summary: A rule a level's room mix keeps (typing.json), over each mission room's tags as its type would give them: its role (role.), its deck (deck.), whether it is on the main path (layout.main_path), and its type's (an archetype's content tags, or type.kit for a room of the kit's own).

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.CameraMath
files.Summary: Camera matrices. Uses the row-vector convention, like System.Numerics: clip = position * ViewProjection.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.CameraView
files.Summary: The camera a frame is drawn from.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Device.ValidationMonitor
files.Summary: Receives Vulkan validation-layer messages, logs them and counts errors, so automated runs can fail if there are any.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.FrameGeometry
files.Summary: Everything drawn on top of the static world in one frame.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.FrameParameters
files.Summary: Everything the renderer needs to draw one frame.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Geometry.EffectBuilder
files.Summary: Collects world-space effect quads (impacts, tracers) as triangles for the renderer. Doesn't allocate after construction. Clear and refill it every frame.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Geometry.EffectShape
files.Summary: The shape the effects shader cuts out of an effect's quad.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Geometry.EffectVertex
files.Summary: A vertex of a world-space effect (40 bytes): a position, a color and the quad's shape.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Geometry.IndexRange
files.Summary: A range of indices in the level mesh, three per triangle.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Geometry.OverlayBuilder
files.Summary: Collects overlay rectangles in pixel coordinates (origin top-left, Y down, as people think about screens) and turns them into triangles for the renderer. Doesn't allocate after construction. Clear and refill it every frame.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Geometry.OverlayVertex
files.Summary: A vertex of the 2D overlay (24 bytes): a position in normalized device coordinates and a color.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Geometry.SkinnedDraw
files.Summary: One skinned body drawn this frame. Holds its mesh (), where its joint matrices start in the frame's , a tint, and whether it's the viewer's own body. The viewer's body is drawn like the gun in hand, in front of the world, so it never clips through a wall the player is standing against.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Geometry.SwarmInstance
files.Summary: One horde body to draw this frame: where it stands and which way it faces, the two poses it's blending between, and how it looks. Matches the per-instance inputs of content/shaders/swarm.slang (64 bytes).

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.GpuDetection
files.Summary: Probes whether a dedicated (discrete) GPU is present on the host system.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Lighting.Atmosphere
files.Summary: How the air between the camera and the scene is rendered. Either as even haze (the level's haze only, the old distance fog), or through a froxel grid over the view, coarse or fine, where the frame's lights show up as light beams and glows.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Lighting.FogVolume
files.Summary: A cloud of smoke for one frame, for example from a blast or a breach. It's densest at the center and thins out to nothing at its radius. The froxel grid adds it to the air ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Lighting.PointLight
files.Summary: A light for the world shader (112 bytes, matches PointLight in content/shaders/scene_lights.slang). A point light fades to nothing at its radius and only lights what's inside its box (a room), so it doesn't need shadows to keep from leaking into the next room. A spotlight (a flashlight) also only lights inside its cone. A rect light (: a panel's glass, a floor channel in a hall, a light strip) shines from one side of a rectangle, as bright as its glass glows, and fades with distance from the nearest point on it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Lighting.RectLights
files.Summary: Computes the light a rectangle casts on a surface, the same way the world shader does (rectIrradiance in content/shaders/scene_lights.slang). It uses Lambert's formula for the rectangle's polygon as seen from the surface, after clipping it at the surface's horizon. This is for tests and tools; the shader is what actually lights the frame.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Lighting.ReflectionCapture
files.Summary: A request to recapture a room's reflection cube map. It names the room (an index into the frame's ), the lights to capture it with (a range of , which don't cast shadows in the capture), and which level geometry to draw (a range of : the room's own parts plus what's visible through its doorways, nothing broken). Characters and effects are never captured.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Lighting.RoomDoorway
files.Summary: A doorway between two rooms (): which rooms it connects and the box of its opening.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Lighting.RoomLighting
files.Summary: A level's rooms, as the world shaders use them for lighting. Holds a grid saying which room each cell belongs to (the station's own layout grid, where rooms are made of whole cells), and each room's bounce light for this frame: the light from its active lights, bounced once off its walls.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Lighting.ShadowView
files.Summary: A shadow map for this frame. Its tile in the frame's atlas matches its index in the frame's list. The level part of the map is cached at and only redrawn when is set (first use, or something in its room changed, like a prop broke or a door opened). It's drawn from the level index ranges [First .. First + Count]. Characters move, so they're drawn on top every frame when is set.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.PathTracing.PathDenoiser
files.Summary: What takes the noise out of the path tracer's image.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.PathTracing.PathPlan
files.Summary: What the path tracer does this frame, from its settings and what DLSS can do here: the size it renders at, which denoiser runs, whether DLSS upscales (Super Resolution) or denoises and upscales (Ray Reconstruction), and whether the camera is jittered for it. Worked out every frame, so a setting changed in the menu applies on the next one.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.PathTracing.PathTracingSettings
files.Summary: How the path tracer works (). Every setting applies on the next frame, with no restart: the render size changes with , which waits for the frames in flight and makes the path tracer's images anew.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.PngWriter
files.Summary: Writes 8-bit RGB PNG files. Good enough for screenshots, without needing an image library.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Post.AmbientOcclusion
files.Summary: How ambient occlusion is computed: off, at half the screen resolution, or at full resolution.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Post.ScopeLens
files.Summary: The scope view for this frame (the Scope parameter of ; docs/plans/weapons.md phase 2, docs/plans/combat.md). The tonemap pass draws its lens over the zoomed scene, with its reticle at the aim point. Looking through a scope's eyepiece (), the lens is that window, and the rest of the frame (the scope's body round it, the world past it) is left as drawn, as Modern Warfare's scopes are. Without one, the lens is a circle of its own and the rest of the screen is blurred and darkened.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Post.ScopeReticle
files.Summary: The reticle shown in a scope's lens (). The tonemap pass draws it over the aim point.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Post.ToneCurve
files.Summary: How scene light, including values brighter than white, is mapped into the display's range (content/shaders/tonemap.slang).

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Rays.RayGeometry.Run
files.Summary: One geometry: a range of the mesh's indices, and the part it belongs to if that part can disappear (-1 if it's always there).

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Rays.RayGeometry
files.Summary: The level mesh as the rays see it: only the drawn parts (collision-only parts are left out), split into the geometries of the level's bottom-level acceleration structure. Parts that never disappear are merged into as few geometries as the mesh order allows, and are opaque, so a ray stops at them right away. Each part that can disappear (a prop that breaks, a door that opens, ) gets its own geometry and isn't opaque, so the shader can check every frame whether it's still there.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Rays.RayQualitySettings
files.Summary: The settings a level controls.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Rays.RayTracingQuality
files.Summary: How much ray tracing work is done each frame when rays are enabled (; docs/plans/ray-tracing.md phase 11). Each level sets the expensive settings together ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Rays.RayTracingSupport
files.Summary: Whether a GPU supports ray tracing the way the renderer uses it (ray queries from compute shaders against acceleration structures). Checks the required extensions and features, and if any are missing, lists them for the log. NVIDIA RTX 20 series and later, AMD RX 6000 and later, and Intel Arc support it, and so does Mesa's software driver from version 25.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.RenderPath
files.Summary: How the renderer lights the scene. Both draw the same level, bodies, effects and HUD with the same post-processing; they differ in how light is worked out. Changing it takes effect on the next frame, with no restart.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.RendererOptions
files.Summary: Renderer start-up settings.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Streamline.DlssMode
files.Summary: The DLSS quality mode: how far below the display's resolution the path tracer renders before DLSS (Super Resolution, or Ray Reconstruction, which denoises as it upscales) brings it up to the display's. Named as NVIDIA's RTX UI guidelines name them. renders at the display's resolution and only uses DLSS to clean up the image.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Streamline.DlssResolution
files.Summary: The arithmetic DLSS needs from the renderer: how big to render for a mode (when Streamline cannot say), how many steps the camera jitter takes and where each one is, and which sl::DLSSMode a mode is.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Streamline.DlssSupport
files.Summary: What DLSS can do on this machine, for the renderer and the video settings: Super Resolution (upscaling), Ray Reconstruction (denoising the path tracer as it upscales), and if not, why not, in words a player can act on.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Streamline.StreamlineCamera
files.Summary: One frame's camera as Streamline's common constants describe it (sl::Constants). The matrices are System.Numerics' row-vector ones, which is the layout Streamline's row-major float4x4 expects, and none of them holds the jitter.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Streamline.StreamlineImage
files.Summary: An image handed to a DLSS feature (an input like the depth or the noisy color, or the output), described the way Streamline needs it on Vulkan: it cannot ask the driver about an image, so the host says what it is, what it can be used for and the layout it will be in when the feature runs.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.Streamline.StreamlineRequirements
files.Summary: What the loaded DLSS features need of the Vulkan instance and device (slGetFeatureRequirements): with manual hooking, the renderer enables these itself when it creates them. Feature names are fields of VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features and VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan13Features, as the C headers spell them.

files.Title: LastFleet.Rendering.VulkanRenderer
files.Summary: The Vulkan 1.3 renderer. It draws the scene in HDR with multisampling (the static world mesh, flat-shaded with a depth buffer and tinted per part, plus the horde, bodies, world-space effects and the gun in hand), then applies bloom and the tone curve into the swapchain, then draws the 2D overlay and textured UI (Dear ImGui) on top.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.ChoirBodies
files.Summary: The size, speed and health of each of the Choir's bigger units (). The host spawns them with these values, and a client builds its copies the same way from just the kind.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.AmmoDrop
files.Summary: Marks a character that drops ammo where it dies.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.AmmoPickup
files.Summary: Ammo lying in the world. Walking over it tops up every carried weapon's reserve by magazines' worth. A crate ( above zero) respawns after a while. A drop disappears when it's taken or when runs out.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.FireMode
files.Summary: How the trigger turns into shots. A gun's comes from its trigger group (see ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.FireModeSet
files.Summary: A set of s: the ones a frame allows, or the ones a trigger group can be switched between. Switching steps through them in 's order (Automatic, SemiAutomatic, Burst, Manual), round to the first, whatever order the data lists them in.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.FittedParts
files.Summary: The parts fitted to a weapon to replace the ones it rolled, one per part slot (barrel, magazine, stock, optic, module, muzzle, grip, trigger, in that order). An empty slot keeps the rolled part. This is part of a , so a weapon a player has modified still only takes a few bytes to send.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.Grenade
files.Summary: A live grenade, in flight or resting (or a placed device), counting down to its explosion.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.GrenadeBag
files.Summary: A character's grenades: how many it carries, and how they recharge.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.Loadout
files.Summary: The weapons a player carries: two of them (a main weapon and a sidearm, or any two), with one in hand. Everything else they carry is in their .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.PartFit
files.Summary: One weapon part as data: which part it is (the hash of its id in the loot data, see LastFleet.Loot) and how well its ranges rolled (0 is the worst of each range, 255 the best). A of zero means no part.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.StatChange
files.Summary: A timed stat change from using a : which stat, by how much, and how many seconds are left.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.StatChangeSlots
files.Summary: The stat changes a player has active (). It's an inline array so the component stays a value type.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.WeaponDrop
