files.Summary: A weapon lying in the world with its ammo. It can come from a loot cache, a soldier's body, or a player who swapped it for another one. A player picks it up by holding Interact next to it (see ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.WeaponFrame
files.Summary: The kind of gun, called its frame (for example an auto rifle or a shotgun), stored as its index in the frames in play (, the loot data's archetypes in order). It's stored and sent as that index, so the host and clients must be using the same frames. The first frame is the default.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.WeaponIdentity
files.Summary: Which loot roll a weapon came from: the seed, loot table and item level it's rebuilt from. That way a weapon only takes a few bytes to send, and the HUD can name it. is zero for a stock (unrolled) weapon.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.WeaponSlot
files.Summary: A carried weapon that isn't in hand: its stats, plus its ammo and shot counter as they were when it was put away.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.WeaponSlots
files.Summary: The slots of a .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.WeaponState
files.Summary: Live state of an equipped weapon.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.WeaponStats
files.Summary: Physical weapon values the simulation uses. produces them from the designer-facing 0–100 stats, so edit the profile, not these numbers.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.WeaponTraits
files.Summary: What a weapon does beyond its numbers (see the design doc, "Manufacturers" and "Rarity and affixes"). A trait can be a manufacturer's signature, or the effect of an affix or a relic. The numbers live in .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.CargoCrate
files.Summary: A cargo crate standing in the world, with its at the middle of its base. It's too big for the pack, so it's carried in both hands (see ) to the extraction for the fleet. A player picks it up by holding Interact, the same as any pickup.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.CargoLoad
files.Summary: A crate of cargo for the fleet: which item and how much. It's either lying in the world () or being carried.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.CargoPod
files.Summary: A cargo pod dropped from a beacon (an item whose effect calls a pod, ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.FleetHaul
files.Summary: What a mission brought back to the fleet: how much of each supply and raw material, and how many crates. It counts what's in the squad's packs, the cargo crates carried or set down at the extraction, and the tanks pumped.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.HaulAmounts
files.Summary: How much of each item a holds, indexed by the item's position in minus one.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.HosePoints
files.Summary: The bends of a 's hose, starting from its valve. It's fixed size so it works in the ECS.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.PipeValve
files.Summary: A valve on a deep reservoir's pipe (): where its wheel is, and where a player stands to turn it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.PipeValves
files.Summary: The valves on a reservoir's pipe. It's fixed size so it works in the ECS.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.PodPhase
files.Summary: How far along a is in its job.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.SupplyTank
files.Summary: One of the station's fuel or water tanks. The tank itself is built into the level. This component is its valve, at the entity's position.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo.TankPhase
files.Summary: How far along a is in being emptied into the docked dropship.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.Afflictions
files.Summary: Damage over time from a weapon trait. Corrosion () deals for seconds, credited to . A fresh hit renews it instead of stacking.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.CharacterBody
files.Summary: Links a character to its collision body in the .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.CommandButtons
files.Summary: Buttons held during a tick. Systems detect presses by comparing with the previous tick.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.CoverKind
files.Summary: What kind of cover a character is behind, which decides how it peeks ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.EscapedTag
files.Summary: Marks a player who got off in an escape pod: sealed in it, out of the fight, waiting for the rest of the squad. The mission and the Director leave them out of the squad.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.Faction
files.Summary: The faction a character belongs to.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.FactionId
files.Summary: Which faction a character fights for. Shots never damage their own faction, but they're still stopped by it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.Falling
files.Summary: Marks a loose object (a weapon, a pile, a case, a crate) that's falling because what it rested on broke (). Holds its fall speed in m/s. It's removed when the object lands.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.HandAction
files.Summary: What a character's hands are doing and how far along it is, as a client sees it for characters other than its own.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.HandActionKind
files.Summary: What a character's hands are doing, so other players can see it ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.Health
files.Summary: Hit points for a character, with Destiny-style regeneration: after without damage, health refills at . A player's effects () can add a shield and armor in front of health, which absorb damage in that order, and can change how much damage it takes.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.LinearVelocity
files.Summary: Linear velocity in meters per second.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.MovementSettings
files.Summary: Movement tuning for a character, in meters and seconds. It's data, not code: roles, perks and implants change these values instead of changing the controller.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.MovementState
files.Summary: Everything the player controller remembers between ticks.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.Ping
files.Summary: A player's mark for the team (design doc: "ping system ... so pickup groups work without voice chat"). It marks an enemy or a place, and shows through walls with its distance until runs out. Each player gets one, so a new ping replaces the last. The entity's is where the mark is drawn.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.PingKind
files.Summary: What a ping marks.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.PlayerCommand
files.Summary: One tick of player intent. This is the only way input reaches the simulation.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.PlayerEffects
files.Summary: What effects are currently doing to a player ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.PlayerTag
files.Summary: Marks the entities controlled by players.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.PuppetTag
files.Summary: Marks a character that's positioned from outside the simulation, like a co-op client's copies of the other players used for its prediction. Other characters bump into it, but the body system never moves it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.Rescue
files.Summary: A player's state for downed, revive and drag (see the design doc, "Downed, revive and drag").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.ShieldGrant
files.Summary: A shield's size and how it regenerates (). An amount of zero means no shield.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.SoldierTag
files.Summary: Marks AI-controlled soldiers.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.SpawnPoint
files.Summary: Where a player respawns after dying.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.Stance
files.Summary: Body posture. Sliding is a timed state entered from a sprint.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.ViewAngles
files.Summary: Where a character is looking, in radians.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters.WorldPosition
files.Summary: World-space position in meters. For characters this is the feet.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Choir.AcidGlob
files.Summary: A Spitter's glob of acid in flight, with its . It's thrown from at on , falls under , and leaves an where it lands. Its position can be worked out from those values alone, so clients draw it from them.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Choir.AcidPool
files.Summary: A pool of a Spitter's acid on the floor. It burns anyone standing in it who isn't Choir, from until . It's there to force players to move.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Choir.ChoirAction
files.Summary: What a is doing, for drawing it and telegraphing its attacks.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Choir.ChoirKind
files.Summary: Which kind of Choir unit a is (see the design doc, "Factions").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Choir.ChoirUnit
files.Summary: One of the Choir's bigger units (Strippers, Spitters, Weavers, the Herald). It's a character like a soldier (controller, body, health, the Choir's ), but driven by the Choir's own simple AI instead of a soldier's. This component holds what kind it is and what it's doing, which the clients can see.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Choir.SwarmSurface
files.Summary: What a is clinging to: the floor, the ceiling (feet on it, hanging down), or a wall it's climbing. Walls are named by the direction they face, since a station's walls line up with the grid. The body sticks out from the surface.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Choir.SwarmSurfaces
files.Summary: Which way is up for a body on each , and which way it faces.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Choir.Swarmling
files.Summary: A horde body (the Choir's swarmlings, see the design doc, "Horde simulation"). It isn't a character with a controller and a physics body. It's a small thing that runs over the navigation grid in large numbers. It also has (its feet), (which way it faces), and .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Choir.SwarmlingAction
files.Summary: What a is doing.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.Container
files.Summary: A container to search, like a footlocker or a case, with its at the middle of its base. A player opens it by holding Interact, the same as picking up an item (see ), and its contents are laid out on top as items to take. Once opened, it stays open.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.ContainerItems
files.Summary: What's inside a .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.ContainerKind
files.Summary: What kind of it is. The numeric values are sent over the network, so add new ones at the end.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.Inventory
files.Summary: What a player carries besides their weapons (). There are four quick slots for consumables used in the field (medkits, ammo packs) and a pack of twelve slots for everything else, except items carried in both arms. Slots are numbered with the quick slots first (0 to 3), then the pack (4 to 15).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.InventoryOp
files.Summary: Something a player does with their inventory, carried in a .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.ItemDefinition
files.Summary: What an item is like (content/defs/loot/items.json): its name, model and colors, how many stack in a slot, what it's for (), and the fields that its roles turn on.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.ItemDrop
files.Summary: Items lying in the world at their , resting on whatever is under them (a floor, a shelf). A player holding Interact next to them picks up whatever fits (see ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.ItemKind
files.Summary: Identifies an item (other than weapons, which are carried in the ) by its position in the items in play (, from the loot data's items.json), counting from 1. 0 means none.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.ItemPile
files.Summary: A stack of one kind of item, either in an inventory slot or lying in the world.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.ItemRoles
files.Summary: What an item is for (its flags in items.json). Each flag turns on the item fields and rules that go with it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.Items
files.Summary: The items currently in play (). Once the loot data's items.json is put in play with , those are used. Otherwise it's the shipped ones (), which match the repository's data. In play, an item is identified by its position in the list (). What a consumable does is defined by its effect ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.LootDrop
files.Summary: Marks a character that may drop a weapon where it dies. The loot system only rolls for it once ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.PackSlots
files.Summary: The pack slots of an .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.QuickSlots
files.Summary: The quick slots of an , for consumables used in the field.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.Breach
files.Summary: A hull breach: a patched plate in the station's outer hull. Like a , it sits on the same entity as an unbreakable (the plate). The horde blows it open (marked broken, collision off) and pours in through the hole behind it, and it stays open. It's replicated through the broken-surface list like any prop.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.BreachPhase
files.Summary: Where a window's breach is (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.ClosetDoor
files.Summary: A spawn closet's door. Like a , it's a level part on the same entity as an unbreakable . It's open (marked broken, collision off) while reinforcements leave the closet, and shuts again once the closet is empty. It's replicated through the broken-surface list like any prop.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.EscapePod
files.Summary: An escape pod's hatch. Like a , it's a level part on the same entity as an unbreakable , but the other way round: open (marked broken, collision off) until the pod launches, then shut for good with whoever was inside.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.HullWindow
files.Summary: A window onto space (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10), on the same entity as its pane's , which holds (takes damage, never breaks: ). Its damage shows as cracks, then blows it out: a breach, which the mission's breach system runs.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.MissionKey
files.Summary: A keycard lying in the level (with a ). The squad picks it up by walking over it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.MissionLock
files.Summary: A locked door: a level part on the same entity as a that shots can't break. Its keycard opens it by marking the part broken and turning its collision off, so clients see it and walk through it the same way as a broken prop. Restarting the fight closes it again.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.MissionPhase
files.Summary: Which phase a mission is in (see the design doc, "Mission structure").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.MissionState
files.Summary: The mission's state, kept on one entity. It's small, so it's replicated whole to co-op clients in every snapshot, and it's hashed in the simulation checksum. Keycard and lock ids start at 1, with one bit each in and .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.ObjectiveKind
files.Summary: What a mission's squad comes for (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "Objective kinds").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.RoomDoorState
files.Summary: A room's own door in a plan's level (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10), on the same entity as its door's : open is broken, as for any door, so clients see it the same way. It slides open for whoever comes near, or () is opened and shut by hand; the swarm batters one opened by hand until it's , open for good. A breach in either of its rooms seals it shut.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.SealableDoor
files.Summary: A door through a bulkhead, between compartments and , that shuts while either is sealed: on the same entity as its door's (a pressure door's, or a gate's beside its ). Open is broken, as for any door, so clients see it the same way.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.WindowPart
files.Summary: One of a window's parts that the mission shows as its breach goes (): on the same entity as the part's , which never breaks but is marked broken while the part is hidden, so clients see it come and go the same way as anything broken.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions.WindowPartKind
files.Summary: Which of a window's hidden parts a is.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.World.Destructible
files.Summary: A level part that can be destroyed. Shots and grenades wear it down. When it breaks, its collision is turned off (so it no longer blocks movement, sight or shots), and a tells the client to hide it and throw debris.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.World.DestructibleMaterial
files.Summary: What a breakable prop is made of. This sets how much it takes to break and what it breaks into.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.World.HullPull
files.Summary: The pull toward a breached window (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10): air rushing out through it, dragging anyone who can see it toward it, harder the nearer they are (). The host's breach system makes one while a breach is open; a client's prediction gets a copy from the mission's state, so the pull is felt without waiting on the host.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Components.World.Target
files.Summary: A shootable practice target made of level surfaces: a body, and a head that takes precision damage. It drops when its health runs out, and stands back up fully healed after .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.CallPodAction
files.Summary: Drops a cargo pod () in front of the player, but only while a mission is still going ("do": "callPod").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.ChangeStatAction
files.Summary: Changes Stat by By, as a fraction of the stat (0.25 is a quarter more). When used, it lasts Seconds. As a passive, it lasts while its item is held and Seconds is 0.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.EffectAction
files.Summary: One thing an effect does (one entry in its "actions" list in effects.json, picked by its "do"). Each kind is its own record holding the values it needs, and carries them out.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.EffectCueLog
files.Summary: The effect cues raised this tick (). It's cleared every tick, like the explosions, and the client plays them.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.EffectCueRecord
files.Summary: A sound or flash an effect made (, ), for the presentation to play. It records when and where, and which action of which effect. The effect is its index in , which is the same on host and clients.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.EffectDefinition
files.Summary: What an item does (content/defs/loot/effects.json): when it happens () and what it does (, in order). A consumable item names one of these.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.EffectRegistry
files.Summary: The effects currently in play (). Once the loot data's effects.json is put in play with , those are used. Otherwise it's the shipped ones (), which match the repository's data. Items refer to effects by id.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.EffectRequest
files.Summary: Something an effect needs done in the world, which the caller of handles: dropping a pod or a device, or playing a sound or a flash. Index is the action's index in the effect's action list.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.EffectRunner
files.Summary: Runs an effect () on a player. It can check whether using the effect now would do anything, and it applies the effect's actions in order. Anything that needs the world (like dropping a pod) is handed back for the caller to do.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.EffectTrigger
files.Summary: When an effect happens (the "trigger" field in effects.json).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.FlashAction
files.Summary: A burst of light at the player's position. Its color is Color (each channel 0 to 1) times Brightness, it reaches Radius meters, and it fades over Seconds. It's purely visual.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.GiveArmorAction
files.Summary: Gives Amount armor, up to Max. If the player already has more than Max, nothing is taken away. Armor absorbs damage after the shield and before health, and it doesn't regenerate.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.HealAction
files.Summary: Heals Amount health, up to max health ("do": "heal").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.PlaceDeviceAction
files.Summary: Places a device in front of the player, on the wall ahead or on the floor. This is the breaching charge.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.PlayerStat
files.Summary: The stats a stat change () can modify. Each is changed by a fraction of its value.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.RefillAmmoAction
files.Summary: Adds Magazines magazines' worth of ammo to every weapon's reserve ("do": "refillAmmo").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.ShieldAction
files.Summary: A shield of Amount that absorbs damage first. It regenerates at PerSecond after DelaySeconds without taking damage.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Effects.SoundAction
files.Summary: Plays the sound Cue (a cue in content/defs/sounds.json) at the player's position, for everyone nearby.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Movement.CharacterMovement
files.Summary: Building blocks for first-person movement: look, directions, friction and acceleration. They're pure functions, so they can be tested without an ECS world. combines them.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Movement.Mantle
files.Summary: Climbing onto ledges, Witchfire style. If you jump at a ledge while pressing forward, the character pulls itself up and over with the weapon lowered, instead of bumping into it.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Movement.PlayerController
files.Summary: The player movement model: run, sprint, crouch, slide, jump, double jump and stamina dash, in the spirit of Destiny 2 and Witchfire. One call advances one character by one tick.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Physics.CharacterMove
files.Summary: Where a character ended up after one move.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Physics.CharacterShape
files.Summary: A character's collision volume: a capsule standing on its feet.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Physics.FlatGroundWorld
files.Summary: An endless flat floor at height zero and nothing else. It's fast and exactly reproducible, so it's used for tests, the headless simulation run, and anything else that doesn't need a level.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Physics.HitShape
files.Summary: The hit shape settings for a character () that aren't already covered by its movement settings: the head sphere's size, how far it sits above the eye (standing and crouched), and how much narrower the body capsule is than the collision capsule.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Physics.HitVolumes
files.Summary: The shapes shots can hit on a character: a capsule for the body and a sphere for the head. They're built from the same numbers as the collision capsule (so a crouched character is a smaller target) plus the hit shape (). It's pure math, so hit detection is exact and deterministic no matter which physics engine is used.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Physics.ICollisionWorld
files.Summary: The collision the simulation needs: moving characters through the level and casting rays. This keeps the simulation headless and engine-free. LastFleet.Physics implements it with Jolt, and is an infinite floor for tests and headless runs.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Physics.RayHit
files.Summary: The first surface a ray hit.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Physics.SwarmVolumes
files.Summary: The shapes a can be hit on: a low body capsule, and a head out in front that counts as a precision hit.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.SimulationChecksum
files.Summary: A stable 64-bit fingerprint of the simulation state.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.SimulationSetup
files.Summary: Builds the authoritative simulation world and spawns its entities.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.SoldierBody
files.Summary: The kind of soldier to spawn: its health, faction, speed, grenades, how hard its guns hit, and whether it drops loot.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.FlatUse
files.Summary: A fixed amount used every jump ("per": "jump").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.FleetSupplies
files.Summary: The fleet supplies currently in play (). Once the loot data's supplies.json is put in play with , those are used. Otherwise it's the shipped ones (), which match the repository's data.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.InContactUse
files.Summary: Used only while the Scourge is on the fleet ("per": "contact"). It's what fighting the Scourge off costs.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.MessageShortage
files.Summary: Writes Text to the jump's log.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.MoraleBonus
files.Summary: Raises morale by Amount. If Ship names a ship kind, it only applies while a ship of that kind is still flying.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.MoraleShortage
files.Summary: Lowers morale by Amount, plus one more for every PerUnits units short. A PerUnits of 0 means there's no extra drop.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.PeopleLostShortage
files.Summary: Kills PerUnit people for each unit short, taken from the transports first. The log names Cause as the cause, for example "hunger" gives "40 people died of hunger.".

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.PerDamagedShipUse
files.Summary: Used for each ship that's still flying but damaged ("per": "damagedShip"). It's what repairs cost.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.PerPeopleUse
files.Summary: Used for each People people aboard ("per": "people"). If RoundUp is true, a partial group counts as a whole one (at one per 160 people, 161 people use two); otherwise it's dropped.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.PerShipUse
files.Summary: Used for each ship that's still flying ("per": "ship").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.ProduceBonus
files.Summary: Adds Amount of the item Item to the stores, like a farm's harvest. If Ship names a ship kind, it only applies while a ship of that kind is still flying.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.RepairShipsBonus
files.Summary: Repairs every damaged ship by Amount condition, capped at full condition.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.ShipWornShortage
files.Summary: One ship (never the flagship) loses PerUnit condition for each unit short. Message is logged, with the ship's name filled in for "{ship}".

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.ShortageEffect
files.Summary: Something that happens when the fleet runs short of a supply on a jump (the "short" list in supplies.json). It scales with how many units short the fleet is. Effects apply in order.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.StockedEffect
files.Summary: Something that happens when the fleet has enough of a supply on a jump (the "stocked" list in supplies.json). Effects apply in order.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.SupplyDefinition
files.Summary: How the fleet uses one of its supplies (content/defs/loot/supplies.json). It covers how much a jump costs (, with the parts added together), what happens when the fleet runs short (), what happens when it has enough (), and where the supply can be found.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.SupplyUse
files.Summary: One part of how much of a supply a jump costs the fleet (the "use" list in supplies.json). All the parts are added together. Each one is a whole number of units.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.WhileShipUse
files.Summary: Used while a ship of the kind Ship is still flying ("per": "shipAlive"). It's what that ship needs to keep working.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.CargoSystem
files.Summary: Handles cargo crates carried in both hands (, picked up by the weapon pickup system). While carrying, the player is slower, can't sprint or dash, has the weapon lowered, and can't use anything else.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.CharacterBodySystem
files.Summary: Moves characters through the level: velocity in, position, collision-adjusted velocity and ground contact out. Also swaps the standing and crouching capsules, keeps a character crouched where it has no room to stand, and keeps characters from walking through each other.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.CharacterControllerSystem
files.Summary: Applies each character's : look first, then the movement model.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.CoverSystem
files.Summary: Red Orchestra style cover for soldiers, and low cover and leaning for players. A character takes low cover automatically when it faces something close by.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.DestructionSystem
files.Summary: Handles breakable props. Shots () and grenades () damage them through this system. When a prop breaks, its collision is switched off so it stops blocking movement, sight and shots, and the break is recorded in the .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.DropFallSystem
files.Summary: Makes loot fall when whatever it was resting on breaks (docs/plans/furniture.md). Every weapon, pile, case and cargo crate resting on a prop that broke this tick (inside its bounds, from its base to a little above its top) starts falling, and keeps falling under gravity until a ray finds something to land on. Positions go out in snapshots as normal, so clients see it fall.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.EffectSystem
files.Summary: Applies effects to players over time ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.GrenadeSystem
files.Summary: Frag grenades. Handles throwing them (a fresh press of throws along the view), flying and bouncing off the level, and exploding when the fuse runs out. Explosions damage the thrower's enemies if there's a clear line from the blast, with damage falling off with distance, and are recorded in the .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.HeldEffects
files.Summary: The combined passive effects of everything a player is holding (see ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.HullPulls
files.Summary: How an open breach () drags whoever can see it: like a wind, a drift added to where they move each tick (), so ground friction doesn't eat it and running away still counts. It's strongest at the breach, falling off evenly to nothing at its reach, only in front of the wall it's in and only in sight of it. The same on the host and in a client's prediction, which runs the same body step.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.IShownCharacters
files.Summary: Where each client was shown the other characters. In co-op the host knows this from what it sent each client.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.IShownHorde
files.Summary: Where each client was shown the horde. In co-op the host knows this from what it sent each client. A client's shots at swarmlings are resolved against these positions, so it hits what it saw (see ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.Interaction
files.Summary: Works out what a player is looking at, for interacting with it. A thing counts as looked at when the line of sight from the eye passes within its radius (treating it as an upright column from its base up to its height) and it's close enough to reach.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.InventorySystem
files.Summary: Applies the inventory actions () players send in their commands to their .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.LagCompensation
files.Summary: Lag compensation for co-op: remembers where every character was at the end of each recent tick, so a client's shot is tested against the characters where that client saw them, not where they have moved since.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.LifeSystem
files.Summary: Handles health over time: regeneration, being downed, death and respawn. A dead character's input is ignored and its collision body is removed, so others can walk through the corpse. Players with a respawn after with the stock kit (). The weapons they found and everything in their inventory are left where they died, for them or a teammate to pick up. Soldiers stay dead.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.LoadoutSystem
files.Summary: Switches weapons. When a command asks for another slot, the weapon in hand is stowed in its slot and the new one is brought up, and it can't fire until its swap time has passed. A reload in progress is lost, like in Destiny.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.MantleSystem
files.Summary: Starts and drives mantles. Runs after the controller, so it can take over this tick's velocity.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.PickupSystem
files.Summary: Ammo pickups in the world. Characters with an leave a pickup where they die, and players who walk over a pickup take it if any of their weapons has room. Dropped pickups disappear after a while; crates respawn.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.PingSystem
files.Summary: Pings. Pressing Ping marks whatever is in the middle of the player's view: an enemy there (with a little leeway, so it doesn't need perfect aim), or otherwise the spot where the view hits the level.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.PodUse
files.Summary: The result of holding Interact at a cargo pod (see ).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.RescueSystem
files.Summary: Reviving and dragging downed teammates (design doc, "Downed, revive and drag").

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.ShotResolutionSystem
files.Summary: Resolves hitscan shots. Casts each of this tick's shots against the level and every living character, applies damage to whatever target or character it hits (including falloff and precision), and records the result in the .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.TankSystem
files.Summary: Handles dragging supply tank hoses ().

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.TargetSystem
files.Summary: Stands destroyed targets back up, at full health, once their respawn time has passed.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.WeaponPickupSystem
files.Summary: Handles everything a player uses with Interact: weapons and items in the world, containers, cargo, pods, supply tanks and the dropship's hold. Most take a press; searching a container and turning a valve take a hold.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.WeaponSystem
files.Summary: Runs the weapon model for every armed character and records shots in the .

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.WeaponTraitSystem
files.Summary: Applies weapon trait effects () after this tick's shots are resolved.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.BreakRecord
files.Summary: A prop that broke this tick.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.DamageProfile
files.Summary: How much a shot hurts, and pushes, at a given distance and hit location.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.DestructionLog
files.Summary: The props that broke this tick. Cleared every tick. The client uses it to hide the props and spawn debris.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.ExplosionLog
files.Summary: The explosions that went off this tick. Cleared every tick, like the . The client draws them.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.ExplosionRecord
files.Summary: One explosion and what it did.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.HandActions
files.Summary: Works out what a character's hands are doing () from its state. It checks, in this order: using an item, throwing a grenade, reloading, and a shot just fired. This is only for drawing the body; it doesn't read or change anything the simulation depends on.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.HitLog
files.Summary: What this tick's shots hit: one record per shot, in firing order. Cleared every tick, so read it after returns. The client draws hit markers, impacts and tracers from it, and co-op will send it to clients.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.HitRecord
files.Summary: Where one shot ended and what it did.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.ImpactRules
files.Summary: How a round's push (a frame's ) moves what it hits, read from the loot data (content/defs/loot/impact.json). holds the values the game ships with. Pushes are in meters a second: the speed a round gives a body, before the body's friction takes it back.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.ShotLog
files.Summary: The shots fired during the current tick. Cleared at the start of each weapon update, so read it after returns. Hit detection will consume it once physics exists.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.ShotRecord
files.Summary: One fired round, ready for hit detection.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.SoldierRole
files.Summary: The squad role a frame gives the soldier carrying it, if the squad has that role to fill.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.SoldierUse
files.Summary: How a frame changes the way a soldier fights with it (the frame's "soldier" data).

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.TriggerGroup
files.Summary: What a gun's trigger group (its trigger part) does to how it fires: the modes it can be switched between and the one it starts in, and its rate of fire and burst against the frame's. The default (no modes) leaves the frame's own fire mode, rate and burst, as a gun rolled before triggers were parts has.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.WeaponArchetype
files.Summary: The fixed traits of a weapon frame, the things that make an auto rifle an auto rifle. The stats on a scale these values.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.WeaponArchetypes
files.Summary: The weapon frames. Each one is an archetype from the loot data (archetypes.json) with its model file, how it fires, its fire rate, magazine, damage, spread and so on.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.WeaponFiring
files.Summary: How a frame's rounds travel. Each value is a firing code path in the game, picked by the frame's "firing" data.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.WeaponHandling
files.Summary: The gunplay model, Destiny style: trigger modes and exact cadence, magazines and reloads, aim down sights, spread and bloom, and recoil that kicks the view and partly recovers. One call advances one weapon by one tick.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.WeaponProfile
files.Summary: A weapon as designers and the loot generator see it: an archetype plus Destiny-style 0–100 stats, and three scales on the frame's own values that weapon parts can nudge (for example a coil barrel hits harder, a drum holds more, a scope zooms further). Parts and affixes adjust these, never the raw physical values.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.WeaponStatsResolver
files.Summary: Turns a designer-facing into the physical the simulation uses.

files.Title: LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.WeaponTraitRules
files.Summary: The tuning numbers behind , read from the loot data (content/defs/loot/traits.json). holds the values the game ships with. Each trait should be noticeable in a fight but never decide one on its own.
